One synbiotic RCT in Long COVID found increases in thalamic choline and frontal white/grey matter creatine following treatment, suggestive of CNS metabolic/neuroinflammatory changes.
Peripheral lower-limb TENS significantly reduced body pain but failed to improve fatigue compared with sham stimulation in Long COVID.
A combined tDCS plus exercise program significantly improved anxiety, fatigue, and quality of life compared with sham tDCS plus exercise in Long COVID.
Standalone auricular vagus nerve stimulation and standalone tDCS interventions did not demonstrate statistically significant benefits over control conditions in Long COVID.
Two synbiotic supplementation RCTs demonstrated significant improvement in post-exertional malaise (PEM), a core hallmark of ME/CFS.
CFS patients reported significantly higher general fatigue scores on the MFI-20 than healthy controls.
Physical fatigue on the MFI-20 was substantially higher in CFS patients than in healthy controls.
Reduced activity scores (MFI-20) were markedly higher in CFS patients than controls.
Reduced motivation and mental fatigue subscales of the MFI-20 were significantly higher in CFS patients than controls.
CFS patients had significantly poorer overall sleep quality (higher total PSQI score) than healthy controls.
Sleep latency was significantly longer in CFS patients than healthy controls.
Daytime dysfunction scores were nearly twice as high in CFS patients as in healthy controls.
CFS patients reported more severe sleep disturbances than healthy controls, hypothesized to relate to impaired parasympathetic/vagal regulation.
Abdominal pain scores on the GSRS were significantly higher in CFS patients than healthy controls.
Abdominal distention on the GSRS was significantly elevated in CFS patients relative to controls.
Constipation, loose stools, and urgent bowel movements were relatively uncommon in CFS patients, unlike classic IBS presentations, suggesting the GI symptom profile does not closely resemble IBS.
Male gender was associated with significantly higher odds of CFS overall in adjusted multivariable logistic regression.
Being single (unmarried) was associated with increased odds of CFS in the overall adjusted model.
Current smoking was associated with significantly lower odds of CFS overall in the adjusted model.
Holding an undergraduate degree was associated with lower odds of CFS in the overall adjusted analysis.
CFS patients with both insomnia and gastrointestinal distress had the highest MFI-20, PSQI, and GSRS scores among all subgroups, indicating a more severe CFS phenotype.
Male gender was associated with markedly higher odds of the CFS-with-insomnia subgroup compared with the overall CFS association.
Smoking was associated with lower odds of the CFS-with-gastrointestinal-distress subgroup and the CFS-with-both-comorbidities subgroup.
Age, BMI, place of birth, family history, and most occupational categories showed no statistically significant association with CFS in adjusted models.

A study reviewed used a Random Forest machine learning model on circulating microRNAs and identified 11 miRNAs (including hsa-miR-28-5p, hsa-miR-29a-3p, and hsa-miR-150-5p) that could differentiate fibromyalgia patients, ME/CFS patients, and healthy controls.

Across the 43 reviewed studies, AI/ML models (including support vector machines, neural networks, and ensemble models) applied to neurophysiological (fMRI), gene expression, retinal imaging, and metabolomic data achieved diagnostic accuracies for fibromyalgia ranging from 82% to 100%.

The review identified that neurophysiological signatures via fMRI, gene expression patterns, retinal imaging changes, and metabolomic biomarkers have been used with ML to distinguish fibromyalgia patients from controls.
ME/CFS patients show elevated IgM/IgA antibodies to LPS and elevated blood LPS, LPS-binding protein and soluble CD14, suggesting gut-derived bacterial translocation.

Sweetman et al found notably elevated oxidative stress markers and weakened antioxidant defense in the peripheral blood of ME/CFS patients, with increased lipid peroxidation and DNA oxidative damage and decreased antioxidant enzyme activity.

ATAC-seq of memory vs naive T cells in ME/CFS patients and healthy controls identified 67,189 chromatin accessible regions and showed upregulated exhaustion-associated transcription factors in CD8+ effector memory T cells, with IL-6, TNF-α and CRP markedly elevated after exercise challenge.

Single-cell RNA sequencing of PBMCs in ME/CFS patients showed increased total T cell frequency with notable decreases in NK cells, monocytes, conventional dendritic cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells.

Monocytes in ME/CFS show excessive intercellular communication to other immune cells via an estrogen related receptor α/amyloid β precursor protein/CD74 signaling pathway, proposed as a potential biomarker.

A multi-omics study found genetic variants in GPR180, NOTCH3, supervillin, HSD17B11 and PLXNA1 correlated with physical, cognitive and emotional fatigue dimensions in patients with non-communicable disease.

Fatigue severity is positively associated with functional connectivity between the globus pallidus and occipital cortex, and cortico-cerebellar network connectivity relates to fatigue perception, implicating a basal ganglia-occipital-cerebellar circuit in fatigue.

A two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis found increased volume in right lateral orbitofrontal, left caudomedial frontal, and right caudal middle/orbitomedial frontal cortices is associated with decreased fatigue susceptibility.
A brain spectral study found decreased GABA and increased glutamate levels, with a decreased GABA/glutamate ratio, in patients with CFS, indicating a neurotransmitter imbalance.
Meta-analysis and animal experiments showed that knocking out glucocorticoid receptors in the mouse brain causes fatigue-like behavior, implicating HPA axis dysfunction in fatigue.
A systematic review found decreased NK cell killing activity and imbalance of T cell subsets in patients with CFS.
Levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-4, IL-5, IL-7, IL-12p70 and TNF-α are elevated in patients with CFS, indicating a chronic low-grade inflammatory state.
Fecal Firmicutes abundance is markedly reduced and Bacteroidetes abundance increased in patients with CFS, with decreased microbial diversity and community stability.
Metabolomic analysis showed decreased gut bacterial production of tyrosine and tryptophan metabolites and decreased SCFAs such as butyrate in patients with CFS.

A large cross-sectional cluster analysis of ME/CFS patients identified five distinct symptom clusters ranging from mild limitation to severe autonomic/immune symptoms and marked post-exertional exercise intolerance.
2-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing showed markedly decreased VO2 max, shortened exercise tolerance time and earlier anaerobic threshold in ME/CFS patients compared with healthy controls.
HRV indicators, including the parasympathetic-reflecting RMSSD parameter, are markedly decreased in ME/CFS patients and associated with fatigue severity.
Multi-omics laboratory studies show increased lactate and decreased glutathione peroxidase levels in CFS patients, suggesting energy metabolism disorder and increased oxidative stress.
Genomic studies found decreased mitochondrial DNA copy number and decreased ATP synthesis efficiency in patients with CFS, suggesting increased genomic instability.
Transcriptomic studies show dysregulated expression of immune- and metabolic-associated genes in patients with CFS.

The BioMapAI deep learning model integrated gut microbiome, plasma metabolome and immune-cell profiling from 249 participants, constructing a microbiome-immune-metabolic interaction network linking SCFAs, γδT cells and IFN-γ to symptom heterogeneity in ME/CFS.
In a crossover RCT of 141 patients with relapsing-remitting MS, modafinil relieved MS-related fatigue and was well tolerated.
Methylphenidate improves fatigue severity, concentration and memory in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
A small-sample study found pemoline had some effect on depression-related concentration, memory, tension and fatigue symptoms, but large RCT evidence is lacking.
Fluoxetine (SSRI) is considered neuroprotective and decreases fatigue symptoms in MS patients.
SSRIs were reported not to be effective for CFS patients who lack depressive symptoms.
A double-blind RCT of 151 CFS patients found rituximab (B-cell depleting therapy) markedly decreased fatigue severity scores versus baseline and versus placebo, with effects lasting months.
A small open-label trial found low-dose naltrexone relieved fatigue in CFS patients, potentially via immune regulation and reduced neuroinflammation, though confirmation in larger studies is needed.
NSAIDs relieve muscle soreness and joint pain in CFS patients but have limited efficacy for core fatigue symptoms.
Coenzyme Q10 may alleviate fatigue in CFS by improving mitochondrial electron transport, ATP synthesis and antioxidant capacity.
Calcium channel blockers such as amlodipine may relieve CFS-related cardiovascular symptoms by decreasing sympathetic nerve excitability, though evidence is limited to small studies and case reports.
Methylcobalamin may benefit CFS-associated fatigue and cognitive dysfunction via improved cell energy metabolism and neuroprotection.

A Cochrane review of 8 RCTs (1,518 CFS patients) found exercise therapy improved fatigue symptoms compared with conventional treatment, but showed no significant advantage for depression or sleep quality.
A network meta-analysis of 56 studies found combined aerobic and resistance exercise, yoga, and regular physical activity markedly alleviate cancer-related fatigue.

An RCT found MBSR produced marked improvements in fatigue severity and sleep quality in CFS patients versus untreated controls, sustained for 3 months post-intervention.

An RCT comparing conventional care plus local cryotherapy versus conventional care alone found significantly higher daily living ability and quality of life scores in the combined group.

Patients with CFS typically exhibit abnormal DNA methylation patterns, which may be associated with viral infection and psychosocial stress.
The regulatory roles of long non-coding RNA and microRNA in CFS have gained increasing research attention as potential mechanistic contributors.
Single-cell RNA sequencing has revealed cellular heterogeneity in CFS, enabling identification of specific dysfunctional cell subpopulations via expression differences across cell types.
Spatial transcriptomics demonstrates tissue-specific gene expression patterns in CFS, particularly changes in brain and immune tissue.

Candida albicans is the predominant causative organism of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis, accounting for 92.5% of isolates, followed by Candida lusitaniae at 7.5%, with most affected women of reproductive age (median 29 years).
Women with recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis show reduced neutrophil activity and altered immune responses to Candida albicans compared to unaffected women.
EDS is associated with serious urogenital complications including vaginal dryness, genital fissures, and recurrent vaginal infections, largely attributable to underlying collagen defects.
A connective tissue integrity defect in EDS may create a fragile vulvovaginal epithelium that facilitates Candida adherence and immune dysregulation, predisposing to recurrent candidiasis.

Ceramides are proposed as an essential lipid barrier component of skin and mucosa that maintain barrier integrity and defend against pathogens, suggesting a novel barrier-restorative approach for preventing RVVC in EDS.
Candida biofilm formation is a key contributor to antifungal drug resistance, promoting recurrence and increasing drug tolerance.

Newer antifungal agents such as oteseconazole and ibrexafungerp show promising results for RVVC, but their use is limited by safety and availability issues, while the NDV-3A vaccine remains under investigation.
No direct clinical evidence for vaginal ceramide therapy in women with EDS currently exists, and subtype-related mucosal heterogeneity may affect treatment outcomes, safety, and generalizability.
96% of patients undergoing open repair for isolated PLC injury with hypermobile lateral meniscus reported being satisfied or very satisfied at a median 2.8-year follow-up.
Median postoperative Lysholm score was 85, indicating favorable knee function outcomes after open PLC repair with hypermobile lateral meniscus.
Median subjective IKDC score was 85 (IQR 77-91), indicating favorable subjective knee outcomes postoperatively.
Median KOOS was 85, indicating favorable knee-related quality of life after surgery.
The Tegner activity scale was largely unchanged after surgery, with preinjury median of 6 versus postoperative median of 5.
No side-to-side differences were detected on dial testing at either 30° or 90° postoperatively, indicating restored rotational stability.
Quantified Rotameter side-to-side rotational differences were small postoperatively (0.6°±2.4° internal, 1.1°±4.5° external, 1.7°±4.6° total rotation), consistent with restored rotational stability.

Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is cited as one of several systemic conditions predisposing individuals to temporomandibular joint dislocation, alongside Marfan syndrome, epilepsy, severe vomiting, and neuroleptic-induced dystonic movements.
The paper cites clinical and radiographic literature indicating that roughly 70% of the general population can self-reduce (subluxate) the TMJ, distinguishing subluxation from true dislocation.

The new lateral-TMJ/MRI classification system showed excellent interobserver agreement between two radiologists, correctly assigning all 50 retrospective validation cases to their proper stage and substage.
The main treatment cohort was predominantly female (113 of 144 patients, ~78%), consistent with reported higher prevalence of TMJ hypermobility/TMD in women.

The authors hypothesize that estrogen-related hormonal factors, together with genetic influences on joint laxity, may explain the higher prevalence of TMJ hypermobility, clicking, and disc displacement in females, particularly during reproductive years.

Across all classification stages, the nonsurgical protocol (joint injection with blood or I-PRF, jaw immobilization, and splint therapy) produced a significant decrease in excessive maximum voluntary mouth opening (MVMO) over 12 months.
The nonsurgical treatment protocol significantly reduced pain scores (VAS) over time, with pain eliminated by 6 months and sustained through 12 months in all groups.
Joint sounds (clicking), present in all patients at baseline, completely disappeared in every patient from one month post-treatment through 12 months.

At 12 months, patients treated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin (I-PRF, used for hypermobility with concurrent osteoarthritis) had a significantly greater mean MVMO than those treated with autologous blood injection alone.
Blood injection produced significantly greater early (1-month) pain reduction than I-PRF, but this between-group difference was no longer significant by the end of the 12-month study.
There was no statistically significant difference between the blood injection and I-PRF groups in the improvement of TMJ joint sounds.
The theoretical risk of bony ankylosis following autologous blood injection into the TMJ is considered unlikely because venous blood lacks osteoprogenitor cells required for bone formation.

A prior randomized controlled trial cited by the authors found that combining autologous blood injection with intermaxillary fixation produced better outcomes for chronic recurrent TMJ dislocation than either treatment alone, consistent with this study's combined protocol.

The Hegab TMJ splint was applied at 4 mm thickness for disk displacement with reduction (DDR) cases and 6 mm for disk displacement without reduction (DDNR) cases, worn for at least one year to reposition the disk-condyle relationship.

Contrary to the common clinical assumption that increased maximal mouth opening indicates TMJ articular hypermobility or dislocation, cited imaging studies suggest the condylar position at maximum mouth opening is not directly related to the magnitude of condylar movement.
Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome is cited as one of several factors, alongside smoking and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, that have been associated with Vanishing Lung Syndrome.

A robotic-assisted left pneumonectomy using a five-port (four robotic plus one assistant) approach was successfully performed to treat severe Vanishing Lung Syndrome after conservative management failed.
The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, with discharge occurring on postoperative day 3 after robotic-assisted pneumonectomy.
The 2D:4D digit ratio, a marker of prenatal sex hormone exposure, was significantly higher in individuals with generalized joint hypermobility compared to controls of both sexes.
In male participants, the 2D:4D ratio was significantly higher in both right and left hands in the GJH group compared to male controls.
In female participants, the 2D:4D ratio was significantly higher in both right and left hands in the GJH group compared to female controls.
The Beighton total score, a measure of joint hypermobility severity, showed a moderate positive correlation with the right-hand 2D:4D ratio.
The Beighton total score showed a moderate positive correlation with the left-hand 2D:4D ratio.

A majority of shoulders undergoing salvage surgery for end-stage recurrent shoulder instability had confirmed Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, with a higher proportion in the arthrodesis group than the arthroplasty group.
Postoperative ASES scores were significantly higher in patients treated with reverse total shoulder arthroplasty compared to glenohumeral arthrodesis.
Postoperative SANE scores were significantly higher in the rTSA group compared to the GHA group.
Postoperative QuickDASH disability scores were significantly lower (better) in the rTSA group than in the GHA group.
ASES scores improved significantly from preoperative to postoperative in the GHA group.
ASES scores improved significantly from preoperative to postoperative in the rTSA group, more dramatically than in the GHA group.
SANE scores did not significantly change from preoperative to postoperative in the GHA group, in contrast to significant improvement in the rTSA group.
QuickDASH disability scores improved significantly from preoperative to postoperative in both the GHA and rTSA groups.
SF-12 physical component scores showed nonsignificant improvement postoperatively in both groups with no significant between-group difference.
SF-12 mental component scores remained stable with no significant change in either group.
Forward flexion range of motion was preserved and substantial in rTSA patients, whereas GHA patients had no shoulder movement, as expected for a fusion procedure.

One GHA patient required conversion to rTSA one year postoperatively due to persistent pain and mechanical scapular symptoms despite good bony union, illustrating a failure mode of the arthrodesis procedure.
Another GHA patient underwent hardware removal and a varus-producing osteotomy 2.5 years after primary GHA due to persistent symptoms and scapular pressure, resulting in symptomatic improvement.

No complications were reported in the rTSA group and no persistent instability or nerve problems occurred in either group, with no statistically significant difference in overall complication rate between groups.

In a subgroup of EDS patients undergoing shoulder arthroplasty from a comparator study, patients with connective tissue disorders appeared more susceptible to postoperative complications and instability.

A giant, mobile, filamentous Lambl's excrescence attached to the left coronary cusp intermittently obstructed the left coronary ostium, causing angina-like chest pain in the absence of significant coronary artery disease.
Surgical excision of the giant Lambl's excrescence with concomitant aortic valve replacement resulted in complete resolution of angina symptoms without coronary revascularization.

Histopathological analysis of the excised lesion confirmed a fibrous strip composed of collagen and elastic fibers covered by endothelium, consistent with a giant Lambl's excrescence, with no evidence of infection or malignancy.

The literature review notes that large or highly mobile Lambl's excrescences are recognized risk factors for embolic events, and prior case reports have described LE causing coronary ostial occlusion and myocardial infarction.
After calcaneal lengthening osteotomy, calcaneal length increased without any deformation of the articular surface.
The pedobarographic Arch Index showed 'almost perfect' agreement with the radiographic lateral talo-first metatarsal angle in classifying normal foot type postoperatively.
The Arch Index also showed 'almost perfect' agreement with the radiographic talohorizontal angle for classifying normal foot type.
The Arch Index was the only pedobarographic measurement that correlated significantly with all domains of the Oxford Ankle Foot Questionnaire for Children.
Clarke's angle and the Footprint Index, unlike the Arch Index, did not show agreement with radiographic measurements for classifying normal foot type.
Among pedobarographic methods, only the Arch Index can serve as an alternative to radiographic measurement methods for classifying normal foot structure after calcaneal lengthening osteotomy.

The authors describe a two-dimensional operative video demonstrating a minimally invasive, midline-sparing, unilateral para-articular approach for surgical resection of a calcified cervical (C5/C6) foraminal synovial cyst.

Intraoperative technique steps included CT-guided localization of the lesion, ultrasonic bone resection to maximize exposure while undercutting the facet and preserving joint integrity, careful dissection from the C6 nerve root and vertebral artery, and en bloc removal of the lesion.
5.1% of patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder stabilization surgery developed new-onset anxiety or depression (NOAD) within 1 year postoperatively.
Prior to matching, patients who developed NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery had a higher unadjusted rate of preoperative joint hypermobility than those without NOAD.
Multivariate logistic regression identified preoperative joint hypermobility as the medical comorbidity with the highest odds of developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Female sex was an independent risk factor for developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery, with women 72% more likely than men to develop it.
Preoperative opioid use was the strongest risk factor for NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Tobacco use was associated with more than double the risk of developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Alcohol use disorder was associated with more than double the risk of developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Obesity was independently associated with increased odds of developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Preoperative headaches or migraines were independently associated with increased odds of developing NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Younger age and higher Charlson Comorbidity Index score were independent risk factors for NOAD after shoulder stabilization surgery.
Before matching, patients with NOAD had a substantially higher risk of 90-day readmission, prolonged opioid use, higher total cost, and higher revision rate compared to those without NOAD.

After propensity score matching on all independent variables, patients with NOAD still had markedly higher rates of 90-day readmission, 1-year prolonged opioid use, and higher total cost than matched non-NOAD patients, but no difference in dislocation or revision at 2 years.
Among NOAD patients, antidepressant use was associated with lower 90-day readmission but higher 1-year prolonged opioid use, while psychotherapy use was associated with lower prolonged opioid use.
Only 21.9% of patients with NOAD received psychotherapy, suggesting underutilization of this intervention.
Fibromyalgia patients showed a significantly higher number of reconstructed tracts in the left trigeminal nerve compared to controls.
Fibromyalgia patients showed a significantly higher number of reconstructed tracts in the right trigeminal nerve compared to controls.
Fractional anisotropy of the left trigeminal nerve was significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients than controls, suggesting increased axonal integrity or structural reorganization.
Fractional anisotropy of the right trigeminal nerve was significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients than controls.
Mean diffusivity, axial diffusivity, and radial diffusivity of the trigeminal nerve did not differ significantly between fibromyalgia patients and controls.
Volumetric analysis of the maxillary, sphenoid, and ethmoid+frontal sinuses showed no significant differences between fibromyalgia patients and healthy controls.

A 6-week inpatient integrative Korean medicine program centered on a high-dose Angelica gigas blood-activating herbal prescription, combined with acupuncture, pharmacopuncture, Chuna manual therapy, and physical therapy, was used to treat refractory fibromyalgia.

Prior to integrative treatment, the patient had a 10-year history of fibromyalgia refractory to multiple pharmacological treatments, including opioid analgesics and long-term buprenorphine patch therapy, without meaningful symptomatic improvement.

A blood stasis pattern, likely associated with prolonged analgesic use, was identified as the primary pathological mechanism underlying the patient's refractory fibromyalgia in the Korean medicine pattern-differentiation framework.
Serum NfL levels were higher in fibromyalgia patients than in healthy controls, independent of age.
In both FM patients and controls, serum NfL levels correlated positively with age.

Among FM patients, NfL levels did not differ between those with normal skin biopsy and those with proximal or combined proximal-distal denervation, and NfL did not correlate with intraepidermal nerve fibre density.
Serum NfL was unrelated to disease duration, pain scores, sleep duration, or cognitive performance in FM patients.
Serum NfL levels were positively associated with disability as measured by the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire.

No exercise arm (progressive strength, constant strength, walking) produced a significantly greater reduction in total fibromyalgia impact than the others, and none reached the minimal clinically important difference of 27 points.
At baseline, the progressive strength training group had a significantly higher impact-domain score than the walking group, a difference of medium effect size.

Constant-intensity walking produced significantly greater reductions in the impact-domain score of the Revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire than progressive-intensity strength training, at both the baseline-to-follow-up and week12-to-follow-up delta comparisons.

All three exercise interventions produced significant within-group reductions in total fibromyalgia impact score from baseline to week 6 and from baseline to week 12, though none reached the 27-point MCID.

All three exercise groups showed significant within-group improvement in sleep quality (lower Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores) after intervention, without reaching a minimal clinically important difference.
All three exercise groups showed significant within-group reduction in anxiety and depression scores (HADS) after intervention, without reaching a minimal clinically important difference.
All three exercise groups showed a significant within-group reduction in the wind-up (temporal summation) pain facilitation response after intervention.
All three exercise groups showed significant within-group improvement in conditioned pain modulation after intervention.
All three exercise groups showed significant within-group increase in cutaneous sensory threshold (reduced tactile sensitivity) after intervention.
All three exercise groups showed significant within-group increase in musculoskeletal performance (isokinetic dynamometry) and six-minute walk distance after intervention.
All groups reported a positive perception of treatment improvement, with no significant difference between exercise types.
At week 12, walking produced significantly smaller right handgrip strength gains than both progressive and constant intensity strength training.
Progressive intensity strength training produced significantly greater increases in knee extension strength than constant intensity strength training over 12 weeks.

The progressive intensity strength training group showed greater baseline sensitivity (lower cutaneous sensory threshold) and a greater change in supraspinatus muscle cutaneous sensory threshold compared to the constant intensity group.

24 sessions of progressive intensity strength training increased knee extension strength by 22.36%, which the authors interpret as bringing performance to levels comparable to physically inactive healthy women, based on a prior comparative study reporting 7.04% lower knee extension strength in women with fibromyalgia versus healthy women.
Overall trial attrition was 28.8% (19/66), with particularly high dropout (40.9%) in the constant-intensity strength training group, which the authors note may reflect differential tolerability.

The majority of participants in each group did not adhere to, or did not report on, exercise adherence during a 3-month follow-up period without supervised exercise, with no significant between-group difference.
A 34-year-old woman with MCAS and a history of multiple prior intubations developed progressive dyspnea and was found to have grade III subglottic stenosis on flexible laryngoscopy.
Urgent endoscopic intervention combining balloon dilation, CO2 laser radial incisions, and steroid injection successfully restored airway patency in the patient's subglottic stenosis.
Postoperative systemic mast cell control was optimized using a combination of cromolyn, fexofenadine, montelukast, and omalizumab.
The narrative literature review supports a mechanistic role for mast cell mediators in promoting airway fibrosis and impairing wound healing, which compounds mechanical trauma in MCAS patients.
S1P2 protein expression in colon tissue was reduced in L-arginine-induced acute pancreatitis with colonic inflammation.
Ketotifen, a mast cell stabilizer, improved survival in the L-arginine-induced acute pancreatitis mouse model.
Ketotifen treatment increased S1P2 mRNA and protein expression, suggesting mast cell inhibition occurs via the S1P2 pathway.
Treatment with the S1P2 agonist CYM-5520 prevented death in the L-arginine-induced acute pancreatitis model.
In vitro, mast cell stimulation led to a 2.1-fold decrease in S1P2 expression.
Absence of S1P2 promoted mast cell degranulation in vitro, indicating S1P2 normally suppresses mast cell activation.
The pressure-induced myogenic response of middle cerebral arteries was significantly reduced in rats after cardiac arrest compared with sham-operated rats.
Contraction of middle cerebral arteries in response to the thromboxane A2 analog U46619 was comparable between cardiac arrest and sham rats.
High K+-induced vasoconstriction of middle cerebral arteries was significantly lower in cardiac arrest rats compared with sham rats, indicating impaired maximal contractile capacity.
Gene expression of the cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase ABL1 was reduced in cerebral arteries from cardiac arrest rats compared with sham.
Gene expression of rho-associated protein kinase 1 (ROCK1) was reduced in cerebral arteries from cardiac arrest rats compared with sham.
Gene expression of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS/NOS3) was reduced in cerebral arteries from cardiac arrest rats compared with sham.
Confocal microscopy showed no significant difference in nitrotyrosine expression in middle cerebral arteries between cardiac arrest and sham rats.
Confocal microscopy showed no significant difference in F-actin expression in middle cerebral arteries between cardiac arrest and sham rats.

The authors conclude that reduced myogenic response, tone, and contractility after cardiac arrest are likely due to impaired calcium-sensitizing mechanisms in cerebral vascular smooth muscle rather than changes in oxidative stress or actin structure.
TvSP stimulation induced time-dependent phosphorylation of IκBα in HMC-1 mast cells, detectable by 5 minutes and maximal at 60 minutes.
Total IκBα protein levels decreased over time following TvSP stimulation, consistent with its degradation after phosphorylation.
Cytosolic NF-κB (p65) levels rose early after TvSP stimulation and then declined at later timepoints, consistent with nuclear translocation.
TvSP rapidly induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation within 5 minutes, sustained through 15 minutes, without changing total ERK1/2 levels.
TvSP induced a time-dependent increase in p38 MAPK phosphorylation without altering total p38 levels.
AKT phosphorylation increased in a dose-dependent manner with TvSP concentrations of 10-100 µg/ml, without change in total AKT.
Pharmacological inhibition of IKK2 with IMD-0354 dose-dependently suppressed TvSP-induced mast cell degranulation (CD63 surface expression), with similar inhibition seen for LTB4-stimulated cells.

Chelation of extracellular/intracellular calcium with EDTA or EGTA markedly reduced CD63 surface expression in both TvSP- and PAF-stimulated mast cells, indicating calcium dependence of degranulation.
PI3K inhibitors wortmannin and LY294002 significantly attenuated TvSP-induced CD63 surface expression (degranulation) in HMC-1 mast cells.
The PKC inhibitor Ro-31-8220 significantly attenuated TvSP-induced CD63 surface expression (degranulation) in HMC-1 mast cells.
TvSP stimulation markedly increased IL-8 secretion from HMC-1 mast cells compared with medium control.
PI3K inhibition with LY294002 significantly and dose-dependently reduced TvSP-induced IL-8 secretion from mast cells.

Inhibition of ERK (PD98059), p38 (SB203580), or JNK (SP600125) MAPK pathways each significantly suppressed TvSP-induced IL-8 secretion, indicating that all three MAPK branches contribute to IL-8 production.

A computational virtual screening of 496 marker natural compounds from the Chinese Pharmacopoeia against the MRGPRX2 crystal structure (PDB 7VV4) identified candidate compounds with predicted binding affinity at the receptor's activation site.

Stable MRGPRX2-overexpressing RBL-2H3 cells (H_MRGX2 RBL-2H3) showed significantly higher PE-antibody fluorescence intensity than non-transfected Mock-RBL-2H3 cells, confirming successful receptor overexpression.
Substance P (20 µM) significantly increased histamine release from MRGPRX2-overexpressing RBL-2H3 cells but caused only a non-significant rise in non-transfected Mock-RBL-2H3 cells.

Cell viability of H_MRGX2 RBL-2H3 cells was significantly reduced after 1-hour treatment with Cornuside (80 µM), Baohuoside I (20–80 µM), EGCG (40–80 µM), and Crotonoside (40–80 µM), leading investigators to restrict subsequent degranulation experiments to concentrations below 40 µM.

(R)-ZINC-3573, substance P, PAMP-12, Baohuoside I, Kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, EGCG, Isochlorogenic Acid B, Baicalin, Andrographolide, Isorhamnetin, Dehydroandrographolide, Chrysin, and Baicalein significantly increased intracellular calcium flux in H_MRGX2 RBL-2H3 cells compared to control.

Baohuoside I, Kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, EGCG, Isochlorogenic Acid B, Baicalin, Andrographolide, Isorhamnetin, and Dehydroandrographolide significantly increased both tryptase and β-hexosaminidase release from H_MRGX2 RBL-2H3 and HMC-1 cells, indicating MRGPRX2-mediated mast cell degranulation.
The MRGPRX2 antagonist Z-3578 (20 µM) inhibited the compound-induced mast cell degranulation, confirming MRGPRX2-dependence of the effect.

Neutral red staining showed morphological signs of degranulation—cell swelling, membrane disruption, and extracellular granule release—in cells treated with Kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, EGCG, Baicalin, Andrographolide, Isorhamnetin, and Dehydroandrographolide (20 µM) and Baohuoside I (10 µM), whereas control cells showed no degranulation.

Combining molecular docking, calcium flux, degranulation marker (tryptase/β-hexosaminidase), and neutral red staining data, 8 of the 22 candidate natural compounds significantly activated MRGPRX2 and triggered mast cell degranulation, while the remaining 14 showed weak or inhibitory effects.
Prior clinical research (cited by the authors) identified Baicalin as a key contributor to anaphylactoid reactions observed with Shuanghuanglian injection in clinical practice.
Prior research (cited by the authors) identified dehydroandrographolide as a potential allergenic component of Andrographis paniculata injection.

The authors describe that MRGPRX2 activation couples to G proteins and triggers PLC-mediated IP3/DAG production, PKC activation, and calcium influx, with downstream MAPK/ERK, PI3K, JAK/STAT, and NF-κB pathways further modulating cytokine production and the allergic/anaphylactoid response.
A systematic review and meta-analysis found IBS patients have significantly higher risk of celiac seropositivity than healthy controls, with similar risk across genders and IBS subtypes.
A fecal calprotectin threshold of 50 μg/g differentiates IBD from IBS/brain-gut disorders with high sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value.
Fecal calprotectin >250 μg/g combined with the Red Flags Index achieves high sensitivity and specificity for suspected Crohn's disease.
Intestinal ultrasound used as a first-line point-of-care test has a high negative predictive value for excluding IBD in patients with IBS-like symptoms.
IBS-D patients show significantly lower fecal loading scores on intestinal ultrasound compared to IBS-C patients, aiding subtype differentiation.
Neutrophil-to-albumin ratio is significantly higher in IBS-D patients than healthy controls, suggesting utility as an inflammatory biomarker.
miR-148 disrupts tight junction integrity and, above a cut-off, differentiates IBS-D patients with moderate sensitivity and high specificity.
IBS patients show aberrant limbic system activity linked to emotional responsiveness, viscerosensory processing, and pain recollection.
fMRI functional connectivity patterns (elevated in medial orbitofrontal cortex, diminished in cingulate cortex/precuneus) differentiate IBS patients from healthy controls with high accuracy.
Off-label ondansetron 8 mg/day improved fecal consistency and reduced bowel movement frequency in a real-world study of IBS-D.
Bile acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine treat bile acid malabsorption, which affects roughly a quarter to a third of IBS-D patients and drives secretory diarrhea via mucosal inflammation.
Loperamide reduces stool frequency but shows poor efficacy for improving quality of life or overall wellbeing in IBS-D.
A meta-analysis of 28 RCTs (2475 patients) shows tricyclic antidepressants significantly reduce global IBS symptoms and abdominal pain, with NNT of ~3-4.
The ATLANTIS trial established that low-dose amitriptyline titration is an effective second-line therapy, significantly superior to placebo.
A 2025 systematic review found no convincing evidence of SSRI efficacy for IBS-D, contrasting with earlier meta-analyses suggesting modest benefit.
Postinfectious IBS develops in 10-25% of patients after acute gastroenteritis and shows persistent T-lymphocyte and mast cell infiltration driving visceral hypersensitivity.
A meta-analysis of 28 RCTs (2475 patients) found tricyclic antidepressants significantly reduce global IBS symptoms and abdominal pain, with a number needed to treat of about 3-4.
The ATLANTIS trial established low-dose titrated amitriptyline as an effective second-line therapy, superior to placebo with therapeutic gains of about 10-15%.
A 2025 systematic review found no convincing evidence of SSRI efficacy for IBS-D, contradicting earlier meta-analyses suggesting modest benefit.

Mechanistic studies show SSRIs enhance gastric accommodation and accelerate intestinal transit via serotonergic neurotransmission but have minimal effect on visceral sensitivity thresholds, explaining limited analgesic benefit.
SNRIs show promise for pain reduction and quality-of-life improvement in IBS, though dedicated IBS-D research remains limited.
Postinfectious IBS develops in about 10-25% of patients after acute gastroenteritis and is characterized by persistent T-lymphocyte and mast cell infiltration driving visceral hypersensitivity.
Mast cells are consistently elevated near colonic nerves in IBS-D patients and release histamine, serotonin, tryptase, and proteases that activate and sensitize nociceptive visceral afferents.

Local IgE production against dietary antigens during enteric infections causes loss of oral tolerance, so subsequent food exposure triggers IgE-dependent mast cell activation and meal-induced abdominal pain; IgE-positive mast cells localize closer to nerve endings with proximity correlating to symptom severity.
MRGPRX2 is upregulated in IBS and may contribute to IgE-independent mast cell activation.
Mast cell activation syndrome and comorbid hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome should be suspected and investigated in patients with refractory IBS.
A low-FODMAP diet reduced mast cell recruitment and activation in IBS-D patients, supporting a central role for mast cells in IBS pathophysiology.
MCAS diagnostic criteria in IBS require recurrent episodic multi-organ symptoms plus mast cell mediator elevation, clinical response to mast cell-directed therapy, or >20 mast cells/hpf on biopsy.
Ketotifen decreases visceral hypersensitivity to rectal distention, improves symptoms, and reduces terminal ileal mast cell counts.
Disodium cromoglycate reduces abdominal pain and improves stool consistency in pilot studies of IBS-D patients, with benefits linked to reduced mast cell activation markers.

A phase 2 trial of the H1 antihistamine ebastine showed significantly higher composite responder rates than placebo (12 vs 4%) in 202 nonconstipated IBS patients, supporting histamine receptor blockade as a therapeutic target.
Gut microbiome alterations affect up to 60% of IBS-D patients, with SIBO inversely correlating with Bifidobacterium abundance and directly with pain severity.
The probiotic Clostridium butyricum CBM588 reduced diarrhea episodes by more than 80%, decreased evacuation frequency by 60%, and improved Bristol Stool Scale scores by 30% in IBS-D patients.
Rifaximin is more effective than placebo for persistent symptoms in IBS without constipation.
A meta-analysis found multistrain probiotic formulations significantly reduced total IBS-SSS scores compared with placebo, though heterogeneity was very high.

Fecal microbiota transplantation shows a paradox in IBS-D: symptom responders had microbiota less similar to donors than nonresponders, indicating microbiota engraftment alone is insufficient for clinical benefit.

MCAS is suggested by recurrent episodic symptoms involving an additional organ system plus elevated mast cell mediators, clinical response to mast-cell-directed therapy, or dense mast cell infiltration on biopsy.
Ketotifen, a mast cell stabilizer, reduced visceral hypersensitivity to rectal distention, improved symptoms, and lowered terminal ileal mast cell counts.
Pilot studies showed disodium cromoglycate reduced abdominal pain and improved stool consistency in IBS-D patients, with benefits linked to reduced mast cell activation markers.
A phase 2 trial found the H1 antihistamine ebastine significantly superior to placebo for composite outcomes in nonconstipated IBS patients, with 12% versus 4% responders.
SIBO correlates inversely with Bifidobacterium abundance and directly with pain severity, with microbiome alterations affecting up to 60% of IBS-D patients.
The butyrate-producing probiotic Clostridium butyricum CBM588 reduced diarrhea episodes by more than 80%, decreased evacuation frequency by 60%, and improved Bristol Stool Scale scores by 30%.

Rifaximin demonstrates efficacy for global IBS-D symptoms through modulation of bacterial populations, while specific probiotic strains such as Bifidobacterium show benefit restoring depleted populations.
Rifaximin was more effective than placebo in IBS without constipation for persistent symptoms.
A meta-analysis found multistrain probiotic formulations significantly reduced total IBS-SSS scores compared with placebo, though heterogeneity was very high.

Fecal microbiota transplantation shows a paradoxical disconnect in IBS-D: symptom responders had microbiota less similar to donors than nonresponders, indicating microbiota normalization alone is insufficient for benefit.
Baseline SIBO breath test positivity inconsistently predicts rifaximin response, and rifaximin improves symptoms irrespective of SIBO status in several cohorts.
A network meta-analysis of 28 trials found the low FODMAP diet ranked fourth for global IBS symptom improvement, with low confidence in most comparisons.
In the same network meta-analysis, a starch-reduced and sucrose-reduced diet ranked first for global IBS symptom improvement.
A modified FODMAP-light approach restricting only fructans and galacto-oligosaccharides achieved comparable FDA-defined response rates with lower implementation complexity than full low-FODMAP diets.

Gluten-free or wheat-restricted diets, pursued by about 25% of patients reporting wheat-triggered symptoms, show unclear efficacy with pooled meta-analyses failing to demonstrate significant benefit over gluten-containing diets.

A randomized double-blind crossover trial found no significant differences in symptom worsening between wheat, gluten, and sham challenges in IBS patients who perceived benefit from a gluten-free diet.

Meta-analyses of controlled gluten challenge studies show gluten-specific symptom responses in only 16-30% of self-reported gluten/wheat-sensitive individuals, with most symptoms attributable to fermentable carbohydrates or nocebo effects.

In IBS patients with comorbid mild-to-moderate anxiety or depression, Mediterranean diet counseling achieved markedly superior GI symptom response versus habitual diet, with added benefits for depression and no change in FODMAP intake or microbiome parameters.
A 6-week UK randomized trial of 139 IBS patients found the Mediterranean diet superior to traditional dietary advice, with clinical response in 62% versus 42% of patients.
A network meta-analysis of 42 trials with 5220 participants found minimal-contact CBT most effective for abdominal pain in IBS, with a relative risk of 0.55 for pain not improving.
Face-to-face multicomponent behavioral therapy and gut-directed hypnotherapy showed relative risks of 0.72 and 0.77 respectively for abdominal pain not improving in IBS.
Telephone-delivered disease self-management and contingency management were superior to routine care among patients with refractory IBS symptoms.
Behavioral interventions can improve quality of life in IBS-D even when gastrointestinal symptom severity itself does not change.

A multicenter RCT of 280 patients with diarrhea-predominant IBS found that 15 sessions of acupuncture over 6 weeks achieved significantly better response rates than sham acupuncture, with benefits sustained through 18 weeks.

High-intensity or strenuous physical activity may exacerbate gastrointestinal symptoms in susceptible IBS-D individuals, as seen in high-performance athletes, whereas personalized low-to-moderate intensity exercise plans are recommended.

A 2025 systematic review of 10 studies with 7441 participants found yoga interventions produced moderate to large effect sizes for IBS symptom improvement, with Cohen's d ranging from 0.37 to 3.60 using the IBS Symptom Severity Scale.

Randomized controlled trials show that integrated multidisciplinary care combining gastroenterologists, dietitians, and behavioral therapists produces superior outcomes in symptom improvement, quality of life, and cost-effectiveness compared to standard gastroenterologist-only care in IBS-D.
The lack of validated biomarkers for IBS forces diagnosis to rely mainly on clinical presentation, limiting patient stratification and targeted treatment.
Serum MRGPRX2 levels were significantly higher in patients with allergic rhinitis compared with healthy controls, as measured by the newly developed sandwich ELISA.
Serum MRGPRX2 levels were significantly higher in patients with chronic spontaneous urticaria compared with healthy controls, as measured by the newly developed sandwich ELISA.

A recombinant antibody-based sandwich ELISA for serum MRGPRX2 showed excellent linearity, satisfactory recovery, low imprecision, and a low detection limit, using antibodies generated against an optimal immunogenic peptide spanning MRGPRX2 residues 289-330.
Low-generation (1st and 2nd) Dendrimeric Antigens (DeAns) failed to induce mast cell degranulation despite being recognized by amoxicillin-specific IgE.
Higher-generation (3rd-5th) DeAns triggered significant, dose-dependent mast cell activation across three cell models sensitized with anti-AX IgE.
No mast cell activation was observed in tolerant controls, unsensitized cells, or with blank (unconjugated) dendrimers, indicating assay specificity.
All five synthesized DeAns generations were recognized by amoxicillin-specific IgE in a competitive radio-immunoassay.

In a passive mast cell activation test (pMAT) using patient sera, DeAns provided complete diagnostic discrimination, with activation occurring only in amoxicillin-allergic patients and not tolerant controls.
Mast cell density in the esophageal papillae and epithelium was increased in patients with erosive reflux disease compared with healthy controls.

The density of degranulated intraepithelial mast cells was significantly higher in subjects with functional heartburn and erosive reflux disease compared with healthy controls, with a nonsignificant trend toward increase in nonerosive reflux disease.
In nonerosive and erosive reflux disease, the density of degranulated mast cells in the esophageal papillae was significantly higher than in healthy controls.
In subjects with functional heartburn, the density of intraepithelial mast cells positively correlated with reflux disease questionnaire (RDQ) score.
Skin punch biopsy assessing intraepidermal nerve fiber density had Class II evidence supporting its use as a diagnostic test for small fiber neuropathy, with moderate sensitivity and specificity.
Additional skin biopsy-derived metrics, including intraepidermal fiber length and inter-fiber distance, were identified as supplementary diagnostic measures for small fiber neuropathy.
Corneal confocal microscopy showed potential diagnostic value (Class III evidence) for small fiber neuropathy but lacked validation when SFN occurs in isolation.
Indirect neurophysiological tests such as laser/contact heat evoked potentials and cutaneous silent period demonstrated variable sensitivity but high specificity for small fiber neuropathy diagnosis.
Laboratory screening for metabolic and immune etiologies identified an underlying cause in up to 64% of small fiber neuropathy patients, though this evidence was mostly Class III.
No single diagnostic test, direct or indirect, has sufficient sensitivity and specificity to serve as a stand-alone gold standard for diagnosing small fiber neuropathy.
All FGFR3-autoantibody-positive patients reported neuropathic pain as their primary symptom.
FGFR3-seropositive SFN patients were more likely to be male than seronegative SFN patients.
FGFR3-seropositive SFN patients had lower rates of comorbid fibromyalgia, anxiety/depression, IBS, and autoimmune conditions (Sjögren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis) than seronegative SFN patients.
Abnormal sural sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) were significantly more frequent in FGFR3-seropositive than seronegative SFN patients.
Abnormal radial SNAPs were significantly more frequent in FGFR3-seropositive than seronegative SFN patients.
Length-dependent small fiber loss on skin biopsy, a hallmark of classical SFN, was less common in FGFR3-seropositive than seronegative SFN patients.
A non-length-dependent fiber loss pattern, suggestive of DRG-level rather than distal axonal injury, was much more prominent in FGFR3-seropositive than seronegative SFN patients.
FGFR3 protein and transcript are expressed in sensory neurons of both rat and human dorsal root ganglia.
Patient FGFR3 autoantibody-containing sera showed positive immunolabeling of rat DRG neurons, unlike serum from a healthy donor.
FGFR3 protein expression in human DRG did not differ between male and female donors.
FGFR3 transcripts were detected by RNAscope in TRPV1-positive nociceptors and predominantly in small- to medium-diameter human DRG neurons, consistently across male and female donors.
FGFR3 protein co-fractionated with NaV1.8, TRPV1, and PSD95 markers of nociceptive nerve terminals in skin synaptosomal preparations.

Intraplantar injection of FGFR3-autoantibody-positive patient sera into rats caused a significant and sustained reduction in paw withdrawal threshold (mechanical hypersensitivity) compared to saline or healthy control serum, peaking at 3 hours and lasting up to 72 hours.
FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera did not alter DRG neuron calcium responses to KCl, ATP, capsaicin, or hypoosmotic stimulation compared to controls.
FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera increased action potential firing (hyperexcitability) in cultured rat DRG neurons compared to PBS or healthy control serum.
Rheobase, the minimal current to elicit an action potential, was significantly reduced in DRG neurons treated with FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera, while resting membrane potential was unchanged.

Intraplantar injection of FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera increased phosphorylated ERK, JNK, and p38 MAPK levels in rat DRG in vivo compared to IgG-depleted serum controls, without changing total protein levels.
CRISPR-mediated deletion of FGFR3 in cultured DRG neurons abolished the hyperexcitability induced by FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera, without altering basal firing properties.
In vivo CRISPR-mediated FGFR3 gene editing in the sciatic nerve/DRG of rats prevented FGFR3-autoantibody-induced mechanical hypersensitivity, while having no effect on basal mechanical thresholds.

Peptide array epitope mapping identified four main FGFR3 autoantibody binding epitopes within the extracellular region (ECR), with additional reactivity in the juxtamembrane domain (JMD) and slight overlap with the tyrosine kinase domain.

In non-permeabilized DRG neurons, FGFR3-autoantibody-positive sera labeled the neuronal surface, confirming recognition of extracellular epitopes, while permeabilized neurons additionally showed intracellular FGFR3 staining.

Peptides mimicking FGFR3 extracellular domain epitopes competitively blocked FGFR3-autoantibody binding and prevented both DRG neuron hyperexcitability and mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo, while having no effect alone.
Juxtamembrane domain (JMD) peptides alone unexpectedly increased sensory neuron excitability and did not affect FGFR3-autoantibody-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo.
Prior clinical studies cited in the discussion found no clear beneficial outcomes of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) treatment for FGFR3-autoantibody-positive small fiber neuropathy patients.
A cited clinical study reported significant improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores in FGFR3-autoantibody-positive SFN patients treated with the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody Rituximab.
No reports to date have detected FGFR3 autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients, suggesting direct central effects are unlikely.

Recent clinical studies failed to detect clear beneficial outcomes in FGFR3-AbS-positive SFN patients treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), suggesting Fc-mediated mechanisms are not central to symptom generation.
A recent clinical study reported significant improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores in FGFR3-AbS-positive SFN patients treated with the anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab.
The authors' prior rat model of autoimmune neuropathy showed that an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody reduced serum autoantibody levels and reversed mechanical hypersensitivity.

FGFR3 was previously found in spinal astrocytes where it contributed to TNF-alpha expression, and its expression was increased in the spinal dorsal horn of rats subjected to the spared nerve injury (SNI) model of chronic neuropathic pain.

A high dose (10 µM intrathecal) of the FGFR3 antagonist PD173074 reversed mechanical hypersensitivity in rats with spared nerve injury, but its known off-target activity against FGFR1, VEGFR2, PDGFR, and c-Src raises uncertainty about whether the effect was FGFR3-specific.
No reports to date have detected FGFR3 autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients, suggesting that direct central nervous system effects of these autoantibodies are unlikely.
FGFR3 has also been described in non-neuronal cell types within the DRG, including Schwann cells, satellite glia, and macrophages.
Prior studies could not correlate FGFR3-AbS levels (titers) with symptom severity in SFN or SNN patients.
JMD peptides alone unexpectedly increased sensory neuron excitability compared to baseline, unlike ECR peptides which had no effect by themselves.

Co-treatment of JMD peptides with FGFR3-AbS was indistinguishable from JMD peptides alone, and JMD peptides had no impact on FGFR3-AbS-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo, indicating they do not block antibody effects unlike ECR peptides.
No significant differences were found in subbasal nerve plexus (SNP) parameters or dendritic cell (DC) densities between BD patients with uveitis, BD patients without uveitis, and healthy controls.
Behçet's disease patients treated with azathioprine had significantly lower total corneal dendritic cell densities compared to those treated with colchicine or biological agents.
Behçet's disease patients without uveitis (Group 2) showed reduced sympathetic skin response (SSR) amplitude in the lower extremities compared to healthy controls.
Cutaneous silent period (CSP) durations and sympathetic skin response (SSR) latencies did not differ significantly between Behçet's disease groups and healthy controls.
The authors propose that the absence of significant differences in CSP and SSR latencies may reflect nerve regeneration resulting from controlled inflammation in Behçet's disease.
Dapagliflozin did not significantly change blood glucose levels compared to saline control in normoglycemic mice, although a non-significant decrease was observed.
Dapagliflozin significantly lowered systolic blood pressure at 2 hours post-administration compared to saline control.
Dapagliflozin significantly lowered diastolic blood pressure at 2 hours post-administration compared to saline control.
Dapagliflozin did not significantly change heart rate compared to saline control despite lowering blood pressure, supporting a sympathoinhibitory rather than compensatory mechanism.
SGLT-2 protein was found to be strongly expressed in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) and nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) of the mouse brain via immunohistochemistry.
Fluorescently labeled dapagliflozin (DAPA-Cy3) crossed the blood-brain barrier and localized to the PVN and NTS in addition to kidney tissue, indicating central penetration.
Dapagliflozin significantly reduced c-Fos expression (a marker of neural activation) in the PVN and NTS on immunohistochemistry compared to control.
Western blot confirmed decreased c-Fos protein levels in the PVN and NTS in the dapagliflozin group compared to control.
Retrograde tracing from the kidney with fluorogold identified pre-sympathetic PVN neurons, and dapagliflozin reduced c-Fos positivity in these renal-projecting PVN neurons compared to control.
Dapagliflozin increased the proportion of nNOS-positive PVN neurons co-localized with c-Fos, suggesting increased nNOS activation compared to control.
Dapagliflozin increased phosphorylated AMPK (p-AMPK) protein expression in hypothalamic tissue compared to control, proposed to link local glucose deprivation to nNOS activation.
Dapagliflozin decreased CRH fluorescence intensity in PVN neurons compared to control, indicating reduced CRH synthesis.
Western blot showed significantly reduced CRH protein expression in the hypothalamus of dapagliflozin-treated mice compared to control, supporting decreased CRH synthesis.
Dapagliflozin reduced the number of VP-positive neurons co-expressing c-Fos in the PVN and suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCh) compared to control, indicating decreased VP neuron activation.
Western blot showed significantly reduced VP protein levels in both hypothalamus and pituitary of dapagliflozin-treated mice compared to control, potentially explaining vasodilation and BP lowering.
After 8 hours of fasting, diabetic patients had significantly higher gastric antral cross-sectional area and calculated residual gastric volume compared with non-diabetic patients.
Two hours after intake of 200 mL of plain water, diabetic patients continued to show significantly higher antral dimensions, CSA and gastric volume than non-diabetics.
The increase in gastric volume from 8-hour fasting to 2 hours post oral fluid intake was significantly greater in diabetics than non-diabetics, indicating delayed gastric emptying in diabetics.
Fasting gastric volume differed significantly across the three HbA1c groups (normal, prediabetic, diabetic), with the highest volume seen in patients with HbA1c ≥6.5%.
There was a strong, statistically significant positive correlation between HbA1c and fasting gastric volume, with GV increasing by 16.12 mL for every 1% increment in HbA1c.
Duration of diabetes showed a strong, statistically significant positive correlation with fasting gastric volume, with GV increasing by 6.21 mL for each additional year of diabetes duration.
Random blood sugar level correlated strongly and significantly with fasting gastric volume, increasing GV by 0.66 mL per unit increase in RBS.

ASA physical status distribution differed significantly between diabetic and non-diabetic groups, with more diabetics classified as ASA II-III, representing a potential confounder for the gastric volume comparison.

Despite statistically significant group differences, only 3 patients overall had a gastric volume exceeding the 100 mL threshold considered to indicate elevated aspiration risk after 2 hours of clear fluid intake.
Local injection of the WNT agonist Wnt3a into the external anal sphincter (EAS) muscle significantly reduced anal canal pressure 8 weeks post-injection compared with saline-injected controls.
Histologic evaluation showed a trend toward increased connective tissue in the EAS muscle of Wnt3a-treated rabbits compared with controls.
Wnt3a-treated EAS muscle showed significant collagen deposition compared with controls.
Wnt3a treatment decreased EAS muscle area and fiber thickness compared with controls.
Phosphorylated Stat3, phosphorylated Smad3, and collagen-4 protein levels showed a trend toward increase in Wnt3a-treated EAS muscle that did not reach statistical significance.
Immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry confirmed increased β-catenin, collagen-4, and TGF-β protein levels in the EAS muscle of Wnt3a-treated rabbits.
Proteomic analysis of Wnt3a-treated EAS muscle showed alterations in pathways related to muscle contraction, fibrosis, and atrophy.

The authors propose that local application of WNT antagonists may represent a therapeutic strategy to prevent anal sphincter dysfunction following injury, though this was not directly tested in the study.
Butyrate produced a dose-dependent increase in acetylated histone H3 in enteric glial cells, indicating HDAC inhibition, while propionate's effect was not statistically significant.
GDNF mRNA expression was significantly higher after 24 hours of treatment with 1 mM butyrate compared to both untreated cells and 10 mM butyrate.
Propionate treatment did not significantly change GDNF mRNA expression at any of the tested time points.
SCFA treatment (butyrate or propionate) did not significantly alter TGF-β1 mRNA expression at any time point tested, despite non-significant reductions observed with 10 mM propionate.
Treatment with 10 mM propionate for 24 hours significantly reduced GDNF protein levels in enteric glial cells, despite no corresponding mRNA change.
High-dose (10 mM) butyrate and propionate significantly reduced TGF-β1 protein levels in enteric glial cells after 12, 18, and 24 hours of treatment, without corresponding changes in TGF-β1 mRNA.
10 mM butyrate significantly reduced TNFα mRNA expression in enteric glial cells after 12 hours of treatment.
Both 1 mM and 10 mM butyrate significantly increased IL-6 mRNA relative expression in enteric glial cells at all three time points examined (8, 12, 24 h).
10 mM propionate significantly increased IL-6 mRNA relative expression at all three time points tested.
Despite mRNA-level changes, SCFA treatment (butyrate or propionate) did not produce significant differences in intracellular TNFα, IL-6, or IL-1β protein levels in enteric glial cells.
IFNγ treatment failed to increase TNFα expression at any tested time point, and pretreatment with IFNγ or LPS did not elicit the expected pro-inflammatory response in this EGC cell line.

Butyrate treatment did not significantly affect overall cell viability, though a significant treatment-by-time interaction showed 10 mM butyrate produced higher viability than 1 mM butyrate at 24 hours; propionate had no significant effect on viability at any dose or time.

Intraoperative botulinum toxin injection into epicardial fat pads during coronary artery bypass grafting significantly reduced atrial fibrillation incidence over three years by suppressing autonomic hyperactivity.
Human ganglionated plexus neurons from patients with atrial fibrillation show enhanced excitability, an adrenergic phenotypic shift, and increased synaptic complexity compared with non-AF tissue.
Variable coupling intervals of premature ventricular contractions increase repolarization dispersion and disrupt sympatho-vagal balance by destabilizing intrinsic cardiac neuronal firing.
ADAMTS16 proteolytically activates latent TGF-β, forming a feed-forward loop with TGF-β signaling that intensifies fibroblast activation and cardiac hypertrophy.
TGF-β neutralizing antibodies mitigated cardiac fibrosis and restored cardiac function in experimental models.
Collagen V expression during post-infarction scar maturation modulates fibroblast mechanotransduction via integrin expression, restraining further fibroblast activation.
After myocardial infarction, IL-27 upregulation in F4/80+ macrophages promotes fibroblast differentiation and collagen synthesis, linking innate immunity to fibrotic progression.
IL-6 and TGF-β signaling in fibroblasts drives α-SMA stress fiber formation and matrix contraction, with IL-6 transitioning from a proinflammatory to a profibrotic mediator as disease progresses.

In type 2 diabetes, oxidative stress, advanced glycation end-products, and cytokines IL-6/TNF-α activate PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, and RAGE signaling within intracardiac ganglia, causing calcium-channel suppression and neuronal atrophy.

Chronic hyperglycemia in Goto-Kakizaki diabetic rats causes marked neuronal loss and ganglionic atrophy in the intracardiac ganglia, disrupting parasympathetic signaling and heightening arrhythmic vulnerability.

Noradrenaline inhibits non-quantal acetylcholine release in rat atrial myocardium via α1- and α2-adrenergic receptor activation, showing direct sympathetic-parasympathetic crosstalk independent of ganglionic transmission.

Low-dose 5-fluorouracil induces oxidative stress, fibrosis, and inflammatory remodeling in the rat intrinsic cardiac nervous system, with elevated IL-6, IL-1, and CINC-1 and reduced antioxidant activity driving neurodegeneration and fibroblast activation via JAK/STAT3, NF-κB, and TGF-β pathways.

Histamine activates H1 receptors on intracardiac ganglion neurons, triggering Gq/PLC/IP3 signaling, calcium release, and TRPC channel opening that enhance neuronal excitability, linking immune signaling to cardiac autonomic modulation.
Intrinsic cardiac neurons expressing calbindin-D28k display lower excitability and reduced N-type Ca2+ currents, with structural features resembling diabetic and heart-failure-induced remodeling.

In porcine post-MI intrinsic cardiac ganglionated plexus, IL-6, TNF-α, and nitric oxide synthase activation drive neuroinflammation, glial activation, and fibrosis, evidencing neuron-glia-fibroblast coupling.
In a mouse model of Kawasaki disease, IL-1-mediated inflammation increases nerve growth factor and promotes sympathetic sprouting and immune infiltration into cardiac ganglia.

In rat atrial myocardium, noradrenaline suppresses non-quantal release of acetylcholine from intracardiac parasympathetic nerve terminals via α1- and α2-adrenergic receptor activation, demonstrating direct sympathetic modulation of parasympathetic transmission independent of ganglionic relay.

Low-dose 5-fluorouracil induces oxidative stress and inflammatory remodeling (elevated IL-6, IL-1, CINC-1, diminished antioxidant activity) in the rat intrinsic cardiac nervous system, driving neurodegeneration and fibroblast activation via JAK/STAT3, NF-κB, and TGF-β pathways with resulting neurofibrosis.

Histamine activates H1 receptors on intracardiac ganglion neurons to trigger Gq/PLC/IP3 signaling, calcium release, and TRPC channel opening, enhancing neuronal excitability and linking immune signaling to autonomic modulation.

A subset of intrinsic cardiac neurons defined by calbindin-D28k expression shows lower excitability and reduced N-type Ca2+ currents with structural features resembling diabetic and heart failure-related remodeling, suggesting vitamin D3-dependent calbindin signaling contributes to autonomic regulation.

Post-myocardial infarction neurochemical remodeling in the porcine intrinsic cardiac ganglionated plexus involves IL-6, TNF-α, and nitric oxide synthase activation that drive neuroinflammation, glial activation, and fibrosis with neuron-glia-fibroblast coupling.
In a mouse model of Kawasaki disease, IL-1-mediated inflammation increases nerve growth factor and promotes sympathetic nerve sprouting and immune infiltration into cardiac ganglia.

IL-1 receptor blockade prevents IL-1-mediated NGF elevation, sympathetic sprouting, and immune infiltration into cardiac ganglia in a Kawasaki disease mouse model, indicating a therapeutic target for cytokine-driven neuroinflammation.

In subarachnoid hemorrhage, CNS injury triggers cascading neurodegeneration across nodose, stellate, and intracardiac ganglia via vagal ischemia, sympathetic hyperactivation, and fibroblast-associated neuronal degeneration, described as 'Burned Neuro-Cardiac Web Syndrome,' extending neuroinflammatory damage from brain to heart via the vagal-intracardiac continuum.

Fibroblast-derived IL-6 acts as a central autocrine mediator of cardiac fibrosis after myocardial infarction, driving an IL-6/STAT3/IL-11 cascade that promotes myofibroblast activation and ECM expansion via PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK signaling.

In type 1 diabetes, significant neuronal atrophy and dystrophy occur within pulmonary vein ganglia, impairing parasympathetic control, shifting balance toward sympathetic predominance, and increasing susceptibility to atrial fibrillation, accompanied by fibrosis and oxidative stress.

In type 2 diabetes, leptin resistance and decreased UCP2 expression in cardiac vagal postganglionic neurons diminish parasympathetic tone and impair baroreflex sensitivity, increasing arrhythmic risk.

In high-fat diet/low-dose streptozotocin type 2 diabetes models, decreased intrinsic cardiac ganglion neuronal excitability correlates with reduced N-type Ca2+ currents, alongside hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, insulin resistance, and baroreflex impairment.
Hydrogen peroxide suppresses N-type Ca2+ channel expression in cardiac vagal postganglionic neurons, reducing their excitability and weakening vagal tone.

Normalization of hydrogen peroxide levels via Ad.CAT (catalase) gene therapy restores N-type calcium currents, enhances vagal function, and reduces ventricular arrhythmogenesis, reversing oxidative-stress-induced neuronal remodeling.

Decreased excitability of cardiac parasympathetic neurons in type 2 diabetes, driven by reduced N-type Ca2+ currents and impaired nicotinic receptor signaling, blunts vagal regulation while sympathetic output remains elevated, exacerbating post-myocardial infarction arrhythmias.

Heart failure induces electrical remodeling of intrinsic cardiac neurons, with reduced N-type Ca2+ currents and diminished excitability demonstrated in postganglionic neurons and confirmed suppression of N-type channel function with impaired autonomic transmission in atrioventricular neurons.

Elevated myocardial nerve growth factor induces cardiac neuronal hypertrophy and promotes heterogeneous sympathetic reinnervation after infarction, enhancing electrophysiological dispersion and vagal withdrawal, a hallmark of heart failure.

Bradykinin produced in inflamed or fibrotic myocardium directly excites autonomic neurons via B2 receptor activation, promoting Ca2+ influx and suppressing M-type K+ currents, heightening neuronal depolarization and firing in heart failure.

Kv7/M currents, which stabilize membrane potential in parasympathetic ganglia, become altered under conditions of chronic cardiac remodeling and inflammatory stress, linking fibroblast-driven inflammation to impaired autonomic regulation.
Heart failure-associated ICNS dysfunction involves altered Cav1.3 calcium channel activity, affecting brain-heart communication and ganglionic excitability.
Central sensitization, defined by a CSI score ≥40, was present in 52.1% of women with endometriosis/adenomyosis referred to a tertiary pelvic pain center.
Smoking was significantly more prevalent among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
A concomitant diagnosis of both adenomyosis and endometriosis was significantly more frequent among patients with central sensitization.
Moderate-to-severe dyspareunia (NRS≥5) was significantly associated with central sensitization in endometriosis patients.
Longer symptom duration (>5 years since onset) was significantly associated with a positive CSI test in endometriosis/adenomyosis patients.
Chronic fatigue syndrome was significantly more common among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
Fibromyalgia was significantly more common among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
Temporomandibular joint disorder was significantly more common among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
Anxiety or panic attacks were significantly more common among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
Depression was significantly more common among endometriosis patients with central sensitization than those without.
Migraine/tension-type headache was a frequent comorbidity (38% overall) but did not differ significantly between endometriosis patients with and without central sensitization.
Irritable bowel syndrome was a frequent comorbidity (19.7% overall) among endometriosis patients but did not differ significantly between those with and without central sensitization.
Vulvodynia showed a strong association with central sensitization, with over three-quarters of vulvodynia patients testing CSI-positive.
Restless leg syndrome prevalence did not differ significantly between endometriosis patients with and without central sensitization.
Multiple chemical sensitivity was rare and did not differ significantly between endometriosis patients with and without central sensitization.
Neck injury (including whiplash) did not differ significantly between endometriosis patients with and without central sensitization, though numerically higher in the CS+ group.

Deep infiltrating endometriosis lesions were numerically more frequent among CS-positive patients, while ovarian endometriomas were more characteristic of CS-negative patients, but neither reached statistical significance.
Infertility and previous abdominal surgery were more frequent among CS-positive patients but did not reach statistical significance.
The paper states that approximately 80% of ME/CFS cases develop following an infectious illness, commonly triggered by viruses such as Epstein-Barr virus, influenza virus or SARS-CoV-2.
Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is described as the hallmark symptom of ME/CFS, involving profound worsening of health after minimal exertion accompanied by muscle pain, fatigue and flu-like symptoms.
Approximately 25% of ME/CFS patients are largely housebound and over 60% are unable to work.
Pre-pandemic global ME/CFS prevalence was estimated at 0.3%-0.9%, and in Germany case estimates ranged from 140,000-310,000, including 70,000-90,000 children and adolescents.
The number of ME/CFS-affected individuals is assumed to have at least doubled since the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, and German health insurance data estimated approximately 500,000 ME/CFS cases in 2021.
Cox and Findley reported that over 60% of severe ME/CFS patients were unable to complete inpatient diagnostic protocols due to PEM, motivating adaptive home-based diagnostic approaches.

NHS specialised ME/CFS services report improvements in individual symptoms such as fatigue, anxiety or depression through cognitive behavioural therapy and graded exercise therapy, but without distinguishing outcomes by disease severity.
Autonomic abnormalities and endothelial dysfunction are increasingly recognised in ME/CFS, but their assessment in severe patients is hampered by PEM risk and logistical barriers.

Evidence of vascular dysfunction and impaired vascular regulation in ME/CFS patients supports the use of EndoPAT (peripheral arterial tonometry) for investigating endothelial function in this population, as previously applied in ME/CFS studies.

Heart rate variability (HRV) measurement, previously used in conditions with autonomic dysregulation and elevated stress (eg, musculoskeletal pain), is proposed as an appropriate non-invasive tool to detect autonomic pathophysiological changes in ME/CFS.

Aptamer-based serum proteomic profiling of 7,326 protein targets identified 1,823 aptamers with significant differences between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls, with 845 remaining significant after FDR correction.
There is a broad increase in secreted proteins in the serum of ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
Intracellular proteins, particularly those derived from skeletal muscle, show reduced levels in the serum of ME/CFS patients.
Immune cell-associated protein signatures in serum indicate immune reprogramming in ME/CFS patients.
Proteins secreted by activated neutrophils are distinctly reduced in serum of ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
Focused analysis of the serum secretome supports intensified regulatory interactions related to immune activity, inflammation, vasculature, and metabolism in ME/CFS.
Antibody-based validation methods confirmed the aptamer-based proteomic findings for a selection of proteins.
