Increased numbers of activated CD8+ cytotoxic T cells have been reported in ME/CFS patients.
Elevated levels of multiple proinflammatory cytokines have been reported in ME/CFS patients in both blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
Whole-brain MRS/EPSI imaging across 47 brain regions found associations between glial/metabolic metabolites (choline, myo-inositol, lactate, N-acetylaspartate) and fatigue severity in ME/CFS.

PET imaging with the TSPO tracer 11C-(R)-PK11195 showed increased glial-activation marker binding in the hippocampus, amygdala, and thalamus of ME/CFS patients versus healthy controls, associated with worse cognitive performance.
Elevated CSF and plasma levels of the serotonin metabolite 5-HIAA have been reported in ME/CFS patients, suggesting increased central serotonergic turnover.

The authors argue that framing Long COVID and ME/CFS as psychologically caused or maintained risks harmful therapies, invalidation of patients' experiences, interference with pacing, and diversion from needed physical diagnosis and treatment.
The authors state that many arguments used to support a psychological contribution to Long COVID and ME/CFS are nonspecific or lack sufficient empirical support.
The paper advocates for caution in attributing psychological causation to Long COVID and ME/CFS and calls for evidence-based, patient-centered psychiatric and psychotherapeutic approaches.
The linear mixed model showed no statistically significant overall main effect of study group (PCS vs. healthy controls) on hand grip strength.
Post-hoc analyses showed significantly lower predicted hand grip strength in PCS compared to controls at the first and last measurement of each of the two testing sessions.

Predicted hand grip strength declined significantly from session 1 to session 2 within the PCS group at both the first and last measurements, whereas no such session-related decline occurred in controls, suggesting delayed recovery in PCS.
The rate of decline of hand grip strength across the ten repeated measurements within a session did not differ significantly between PCS and control groups or by session.
Group differences in predicted hand grip strength between PCS and controls were significant at age 55 for both sexes but not at age 25, indicating an age-dependent impairment in PCS.
Within the control group, males had significantly higher predicted hand grip strength than females at both ages, whereas this expected sex difference was absent within the PCS group.

Within the control group, males showed a significant age-related decline in predicted hand grip strength between age 25 and 55, whereas this decline was not statistically significant within the PCS group.

The linear mixed model explained 94.3% of total variance in hand grip strength, with fixed effects accounting for 62.1% and subject-specific random effects for 32.2%, indicating substantial between-subject variability.

Sensitivity analyses showed the estimated effect of study group on hand grip strength was reduced and lost statistical significance after full adjustment for age and sex, although the direction of effect remained consistent, suggesting demographic confounding.

In female participants, higher maximum grip strength in the first session (Fmax1) was significantly associated with lower odds of belonging to the PCS group, achieving the highest bootstrap-validated classification accuracy among tested parameters.

Lower minimum grip strength in session 2 (Fmin2) was significantly associated with higher odds of belonging to the PCS group in female participants, with the second-highest bootstrap-validated classification accuracy.

Previously proposed HGS fatigue and recovery ratio parameters showed poor bootstrap-validated predictive performance for distinguishing PCS from controls, near chance level, contrasting with their proposed diagnostic utility in prior ME/CFS studies.

HGS parameters derived from minimum, maximum, and mean force values showed moderate positive correlations with functional status (Bell Score) and moderate negative correlations with ME/CFS symptom burden (fulfilled CCC items).
Functional status assessed by the Bell Score was markedly lower in the PCS group than in healthy controls, indicating greater disability.
Seven of 19 PCS participants fulfilled Canadian Consensus Criteria for ME/CFS, compared with none of the 23 healthy controls.

Citing prior MRI work, the authors note elevated skeletal muscle sodium content in ME/CFS patients versus controls, proposed to reflect muscle hypoperfusion and impaired ion transport as a possible mechanism for reduced grip strength.

The discussion cites a small-scale study in which creatine supplementation led to a significant increase in hand grip strength in ME/CFS patients, illustrating HGS as a tool to track intervention response.
The linear mixed model showed hand grip strength was significantly influenced by testing session, measurement number, age, and sex, independent of PCS status.

A patient's persistently low CD57 lymphocyte count, initially interpreted as evidence of chronic Lyme disease, did not change after seven months of rotating antibiotic therapy and did not predict subsequent clinical worsening as the treating physician had warned.
SYN1 showed the greatest degree of molecular mimicry among CNS proteins tested, sharing 13 pentapeptides with EBV and HHV-6 viral antigens including EBNA1, EBNA6, LMP1, and EA-D.
Myelin-associated glycoprotein shared 12 pentapeptides with EBV/HHV-6 antigens, indicating potential immune cross-reactivity.
Myelin basic protein shared 9 pentapeptides with EBV/HHV-6 antigens, indicating potential immune cross-reactivity.
Myelin-oligodendrocyte glycoprotein shared 5 pentapeptides with EBV/HHV-6 antigens, indicating potential immune cross-reactivity.
A total of 91 mimicry pentapeptides (42 from EBV, 49 from HHV-6) were identified shared between viral antigens and 10 CNS proteins.
In a mouse CFS model, the three-year-cultivated D. officinale extract (3DOE) reduced anal temperature compared with the one-year-cultivated extract (1DOE).
3DOE prolonged forced swimming time relative to 1DOE, indicating reduced fatigue-like behavior in the CFS mouse model.
3DOE treatment decreased plasma LDH levels and liver index compared with 1DOE in the CFS mouse model.
3DOE lowered plasma cAMP levels and the cAMP/cGMP ratio relative to 1DOE in CFS model mice.
3DOE mitigated renal inflammatory infiltration in the CFS mouse model compared with 1DOE.
Plasma metabolomic pathway analysis showed that 3DOE alleviated energy metabolism dysregulation by enhancing energy metabolism and promoting oxidative utilization of fatty acids and proteins.
Principal component analysis showed distinct clustering of serum phosphoproteomic profiles among healthy controls, LSDP, and QBDP CFS patients, with consistent biological replicates.
The comparison between healthy controls and LSDP patients yielded the largest number of differentially phosphorylated sites and proteins, with a balanced ratio of upregulated to downregulated events.
The comparison between healthy controls and QBDP patients was dominated by phosphorylation upregulation, accounting for the majority of differentially phosphorylated sites.
The comparison between QBDP and LSDP patients showed a higher proportion of downregulated differentially phosphorylated sites compared to upregulated ones.
Upregulated differentially phosphorylated proteins in the HC vs. LSDP comparison were primarily enriched in MAPK signaling and cytoskeletal remodeling pathways.
Downregulated differentially phosphorylated proteins in the HC vs. LSDP comparison were enriched in pathways related to neurodegenerative diseases and nucleocytoplasmic transport.
A candidate differentially phosphorylated site on DENND3 at serine 472 showed moderate discriminatory power between CFS TCM pattern groups.
More than half of patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had at least one chronic overlapping pain condition, with nearly a quarter having multiple such conditions.
Chronic low back pain was the most prevalent chronic overlapping pain condition among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
Fibromyalgia was the second most prevalent chronic overlapping pain condition among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
Women with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had a higher prevalence of chronic overlapping pain conditions than men.
Adults aged 31 to 50 years with autoimmune rheumatic diseases had the highest prevalence of chronic overlapping pain conditions.
Fibromyalgia and chronic low back pain co-occurred more frequently than expected by chance in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
Migraine and chronic low back pain co-occurred more frequently than expected by chance in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
Urologic chronic pelvic pain and vulvodynia showed a strong bidirectional association in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
The review reports that placental extract formulations (e.g., Laennec, porcine-derived) were associated with relief of chronic fatigue syndrome symptoms in preclinical/clinical studies surveyed.

In multivariable logistic regression, having hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome/hypermobility spectrum disorder was not significantly associated with a diagnosis of esophageal dysmotility on high-resolution manometry compared with non-hypermobile patient controls.

The proportion of patients diagnosed with Lyon v2.0 gastroesophageal reflux disease on 24-hour pH-impedance monitoring did not significantly differ between hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome/hypermobility spectrum disorder patients (26.3%) and non-hypermobile patient controls (33.0%).

Among hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome/hypermobility spectrum disorder patients undergoing manometry for dysphagia, normal esophageal motility (61.9%) was the most common Chicago v4.0 diagnosis, followed by ineffective esophageal motility (29.1%).

Among hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome/hypermobility spectrum disorder patients with reflux symptoms who underwent 24-hour pH-impedance monitoring, Rome IV functional heartburn was the most common diagnosis (62.5%).

A nurse's first-person narrative describes her own journey to being diagnosed with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, illustrating how clinical assumptions and limited provider understanding contributed to misdiagnosis and patient harm.
The piece describes a growing disconnect between healthcare providers and patients with hEDS in a rural care setting.
The author recommends strengthening humanistic clinical practice through intentional listening, self-reflection, and collaborative patient-centered decision-making to improve care for hEDS patients.
Nine of 28 pediatric hEDS patients (32%) exhibited mitral valve prolapse.
Aortic root and ascending aorta Z-scores, though within normal range, were significantly higher in hEDS patients than in healthy controls.
Tissue Doppler Imaging showed significantly reduced late diastolic septal myocardial velocities in hEDS patients compared to controls.
Speckle Tracking Echocardiography showed significantly reduced global longitudinal strain values in hEDS patients despite preserved ejection fraction, indicating subclinical myocardial dysfunction.
Left ventricular ejection fraction was preserved and did not differ significantly in hEDS patients compared to controls.
hEDS diagnosis was independently correlated with reduced GLS after adjustment, but not with ejection fraction.
Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic splice-site variant in COL3A1, confirming the diagnosis of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
This is the first reported case of genetically confirmed vEDS presenting with stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, representing a novel association not previously described.
Troponin I was markedly elevated at presentation, consistent with acute myocardial injury preceding the stress cardiomyopathy diagnosis.
BNP was markedly elevated and disproportionately high relative to troponin, a pattern supporting the diagnosis of stress cardiomyopathy over acute coronary syndrome.
Echocardiography showed left ventricular wall thickening, dyssynchronous contraction, mild-moderate apical ballooning, and pericardial effusion, findings consistent with stress cardiomyopathy.

Prior studies cited in the discussion found that vEDS patients exhibit significantly elevated plasma TGF-β1 and TGF-β2 levels, though downstream canonical TGF-β signalling appeared unaltered, suggesting the elevation reflects chronic vascular injury rather than active pathological signalling.
vEDS patients show upregulation of inflammatory markers MCP-1 and CRP, providing direct evidence of systemic inflammatory activation that could predispose to cardiac complications.

Type III collagen constitutes about 11% of total myocardial collagen and contributes to elasticity and mechanical force transmission, while type I collagen (85%) provides tensile strength, together maintaining normal myocardial compliance.

In dilated cardiomyopathy, myocardial fibrosis is characterized by increased type I collagen accumulation with relatively decreased type III collagen deposition, fundamentally altering the collagen I/III ratio.

Animal studies demonstrated that cardiac overexpression of type III collagen improves cardiac function by restoring collagen distribution balance, supporting a mechanistic link between collagen III deficiency and cardiac dysfunction.

Conservative management with valsartan for blood pressure control and metoprolol extended-release plus ivabradine for heart rate control, avoiding invasive procedures and anticoagulation, was followed by declining troponin I and echocardiographic improvement of stress cardiomyopathy.
The patient's father and two paternal uncles died suddenly before age 50, suggesting a familial pattern of early cardiovascular mortality consistent with underlying vEDS.

Coronary angiography showed normal coronary anatomy with TIMI grade 3 flow, excluding acute coronary syndrome and supporting a diagnosis of stress cardiomyopathy rather than ischemic myocardial infarction.

Physical examination revealed characteristic vEDS features including thin lips, small earlobes, midface hypoplasia, skin hyperextensibility, and spontaneous bruising, plus a history of spontaneous pneumothorax, an established early warning sign of vEDS.

The patient presented with a multisystem vascular catastrophe including a ruptured hepatic artery aneurysm, bilateral renal artery dissections with infarction, and a left iliac artery dissection, reflecting the vascular fragility characteristic of vEDS.
A novel frameshift variant in COL3A1 was identified in a patient with an attenuated vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome phenotype presenting with asymptomatic pulmonary nodules and cavitary lesions.

The patient had asymptomatic, fluctuating pulmonary nodules and cavitary lesions as the initial and isolated presentation of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, with histopathology showing nodular fibrosis, focal pulmonary ossification, disrupted pulmonary architecture, and pulmonary hemosiderosis.

The authors emphasize that isolated pulmonary manifestations can be a diagnostically significant, though rare, initial presentation of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome even in asymptomatic individuals.

The patient had a genetically confirmed pathogenic mutation in CHST14, causing musculocontractural Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (mcEDS), a rare condition marked by connective tissue fragility and vascular vulnerability.

The patient had recurrent, disproportionate large hematomas after trivial trauma, including two prior scalp/subgaleal hematomas requiring surgical evacuation, in the absence of coagulopathy, illustrating a recurring bleeding phenotype in mcEDS.

Following a minor fall, the patient developed a rapidly expanding circumferential right lower-limb hematoma (~1 L) with extensive nonviable skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, and focal muscle necrosis, requiring emergent surgical exploration.

A staged surgical strategy—hematoma evacuation, serial debridement, negative-pressure wound therapy, and delayed split-thickness skin grafting—successfully achieved limb salvage with complete graft take and no complications at 17-day discharge.

The authors note clinical heterogeneity in mcEDS hemorrhagic presentations, citing a prior 6-year-old boy with mcEDS whose giant lower-limb hematoma after minor trauma was managed conservatively with compression and tranexamic acid, unlike the current case which required surgery.

A separate cited report described a 26-year-old man with mcEDS who developed a massive subcutaneous hematoma with arterial bleeding extending from lumbar region to scapula, leading to hypovolemic shock, initially managed conservatively but later requiring emergency surgical evacuation after expansion.
The authors state that delayed management of EDS-related hemorrhage may cause compartment syndrome, infection, sepsis, or death, citing a reported fatal septicemia from untreated scalp hemorrhage.
vEDS in this cohort was caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in COL3A1, consistent with the known genetic basis of the disorder.

In this Japanese cohort of 26 vEDS patients treated with celiprolol, 11 experienced vascular events, 14 remained event-free, and one patient died of hepatic artery rupture over a mean follow-up of 96.6 months.
No significant association was found between genotype and the occurrence of vascular events among celiprolol-treated vEDS patients.
No significant association was found between celiprolol dose and the occurrence of vascular events in this cohort.
Semi-structured interviews with 11 patients found that celiprolol use provided emotional reassurance and encouraged a more proactive approach to disease self-management.
Chst14-/- mice had significantly and consistently lower body weight than WT mice from 8 to 52 weeks of age, indicating growth impairment associated with DS deficiency.
The ratio of food intake to body weight was significantly reduced in Chst14-/- mice from 11 to 13 weeks of age, occurring after the body weight difference was already established.
Chst14 mRNA was undetectable in the femurs of Chst14-/- mice, confirming loss of gene expression at the bone tissue level.
Expression of the related sulfotransferase genes Chst11 and Chst12 did not differ significantly between Chst14-/- and WT femurs, indicating no compensatory transcriptional upregulation.

DS disaccharides were undetectable in tibial bone of Chst14-/- mice at 12 weeks of age, confirming that systemic DS depletion extends to bone, where DS normally comprises only about 2% of total GAGs versus ~80% in skin.
Total CS disaccharide content in tibias did not differ significantly between Chst14-/- and WT mice at 12 weeks, indicating CS remains the predominant bone GAG despite DS loss.

Chst14-/- mice developed progressively worsening thoracolumbar kyphosis, with significantly greater Cobb angles than WT mice from 12 to 52 weeks, while WT mice showed no progressive spinal deformity up to middle age.
Chst14-/- mice showed an increased angle and wider space between the femoral head and greater trochanter at 8, 12, and 52 weeks, indicating an early, likely congenital, proximal femoral deformity.
Femoral length was significantly decreased in Chst14-/- mice at 12 and 52 weeks, while femoral weight was significantly decreased only at 12 weeks.

In three-point bending tests, the maximum load femurs could withstand before breaking was lower in 52-week-old Chst14-/- mice than in age-matched WT mice, though maximum load increased with age in both genotypes.

Femoral stiffness (load-to-displacement ratio in the elastic region) was significantly lower in 12-week-old Chst14-/- mice than in WT mice, though it increased with age in both groups and no longer differed at 52 weeks.
Breaking displacement (displacement at fracture) was significantly decreased in Chst14-/- mice and showed a decreasing trend in WT mice at 52 weeks compared with 12 weeks.

Breaking energy (area under the load-displacement curve to fracture) significantly decreased with age in both Chst14-/- and WT mice, indicating age-related reduction in bone toughness in both genotypes.
Proximal femoral cancellous bone density and trabecular area ratio were significantly lower in Chst14-/- mice than WT mice at 8, 12, and 52 weeks, indicating early-onset trabecular bone deficits.

Cancellous bone density increased at 12 weeks in both genotypes, but only Chst14-/- mice showed a significant subsequent decrease by 52 weeks, indicating an age-related decline specific to DS-deficient bone.

The trabecular area ratio increased significantly at 12 weeks in WT mice but not in Chst14-/- mice, and decreased significantly by 52 weeks in both groups, suggesting impaired early trabecular development in DS-deficient bone.

Serum calcium, inorganic phosphate, and estradiol levels did not differ significantly between Chst14-/- and WT mice regardless of genotype or age, arguing against mineral or sex-hormone dysregulation as the cause of bone changes.
Bone calcium and phosphorous content increased significantly with age only in Chst14-/- mice, although absolute levels did not differ from WT mice at matched ages.

Transmission electron microscopy showed that collagen fibril bundle architecture in femoral cortical bone was disrupted, with fibrils protruding from bundles and less uniform alignment, only in 52-week-old Chst14-/- mice and not in WT or younger Chst14-/- mice.
Col1a1 gene expression in femur was significantly but modestly lower at 52 weeks than at 12 weeks in Chst14-/- mice, with only a non-significant downward trend in WT mice.
Gene expression of decorin (Dcn) and biglycan (Bgn), the core proteins of representative DS-proteoglycans, did not differ significantly with age or genotype in femur.

In Chst14-/- mice, the osteoblast marker Bglap decreased and the osteoclast marker Acp5 increased significantly from 12 to 52 weeks, whereas neither showed significant age-dependent change in WT mice.

Rank gene expression significantly increased with age in Chst14-/- mice but not in WT mice, and was significantly higher in Chst14-/- mice than WT mice at 52 weeks, suggesting local upregulation of osteoclast differentiation signaling.
Rankl and Opg gene expression in femur did not show significant changes with genotype or age.
Cathepsin K (Ctsk) gene expression in femur did not show significant changes regardless of genotype or age.
Serum TRACP-5b, a systemic bone resorption marker, did not differ significantly by genotype or age, contrasting with local upregulation of osteoclast-related genes seen in bone tissue.

Square-wave voltammetry of DNA extracted from mdx (dystrophin-deficient) mouse leg muscle showed a significantly lower oxidation peak current than wild-type DNA, consistent with reduced guanine content.
In the col5a1(+/-) EDS mouse model, SWV peak currents were markedly reduced in leg muscle DNA (SOL and EDL) compared to wild-type, indicating decreased guanine content, averaging around 30% decline.
Diaphragm (DIA) DNA from col5a1(+/-) mice showed a smaller but statistically significant decrease in peak oxidation current compared to wild-type, less pronounced than in leg muscles.

LC-MS/MS base composition analysis of mdx skeletal muscle DNA showed decreased guanine and cytosine content with concurrent increases in adenine and thymine content compared to wild-type, consistent with G:C to A:T transitions.
8-oxoG oxidative lesion levels were increased in mdx mouse leg muscle DNA compared to wild-type, indicating elevated oxidative damage.
FapyA, an oxidative adenine lesion, was significantly increased in mdx mouse DNA compared to wild-type, suggesting a more complex oxidative damage pathway beyond guanine oxidation.
In col5a1(+/-) Het mice, guanine and cytosine content was consistently decreased across all three muscle types (DIA, SOL, EDL) relative to WT, with the smallest change seen in DIA.

In col5a1(+/-) leg muscles (SOL and EDL), 8-oxoG oxidative lesion levels decreased in parallel with the guanine/cytosine decline, a pattern distinct from the mdx model, suggesting a different or additional mutagenic process beyond oxidative damage alone.
Approximately 58% of COL5A1 genes sequenced from patients with EDS harbor pathogenic variants, as reported in cited prior literature.
A cited genetic study of Australian football players found a strong correlation between a COL5A1 single nucleotide polymorphism and severity/function of muscle injury.
A diagnosis of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome was an independent predictor of failure to achieve symptom resolution after laparoscopic duodenal lowering for SMAS on both univariate and multivariate analysis.
Laparoscopic duodenal lowering resulted in symptom resolution in 60% of patients (12/20) who underwent it as a first surgical approach for SMAS.
Patients undergoing surgery for SMAS had a narrowed median aorto-SMA angle of 16°, with some as narrow as 10°, consistent with the vascular compression mechanism of SMAS.
Aside from Ehlers-Danlos syndrome diagnosis, no other clinical or demographic characteristics were significant predictors of surgical symptom resolution.
The helical Lapidus plate produced its highest micro-deformation in the first metatarsal of the implanted cadaveric foot.
The plantar Lapidus plate produced its highest micro-deformation in the fifth metatarsal of the implanted cadaveric foot.
Numerical (computational) modeling results agreed closely with the experimental cadaveric test results.
Lapidus arthrodesis with plate fixation corrected hallux hypermobility by up to 82.28%.
Bone failure occurred at a higher applied force (425 N) at the helical plate insertion compared to the plantar plate insertion (275 N).

The helical Lapidus plate configuration was found to be structurally and functionally superior to the plantar-only configuration, with multi-planar fixation providing better mechanical stability than single-plane fixation.
Hypovitaminosis D (serum 25(OH)D <30 ng/mL) was found in 53.7% of adults presenting with generalized aches.
Vitamin D insufficiency (25(OH)D 20-30 ng/mL) was present in 21.3% of the study population.
Vitamin D deficiency (25(OH)D <20 ng/mL) was present in 32.4% of the study population.
Among those with hypovitaminosis D, the mean serum 25(OH)D level was 18.40±5.51 ng/mL (range 6.9-29 ng/mL).
Benign joint hypermobility syndrome (BJHS) was the most common single rheumatic diagnosis causing generalized aches besides hypovitaminosis D.
Hypovitaminosis D/BJHS overlap was the most common combination among cases where hypovitaminosis D co-occurred with a rheumatic disease.
No cases of infection, diabetes mellitus, or thyroid disorder were identified as causes of generalized aches in this cohort.
Female sex was strongly overrepresented among patients with generalized aches and among those with hypovitaminosis D.
Fibromyalgia patients showed a higher prevalence of AOC1 variants associated with reduced DAO activity compared to the general Spanish population.
Four AOC1 SNPs showed differing minor allele frequencies among fibromyalgia patients, with rs10156191 and rs1049793 most common and rs1049742 least common but most catalytically impactful.
Cumulative AOC1 risk alleles showed a dose-dependent relationship with fibromyalgia severity, with FIQ scores rising by approximately 7 points per additional risk allele.
A population genetics study of healthy Spanish newborns established a 66% baseline prevalence of at least one DAO-deficiency-associated AOC1 variant.

DAO-deficiency-associated AOC1 variants show varying prevalence across other conditions (ADHD, insomnia, histamine intolerance), suggesting DAO deficiency may be a shared, non-specific vulnerability factor rather than fibromyalgia-specific.
Studies examining serum DAO enzyme activity have consistently found it reduced in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls.
In an RCT, DAO supplementation significantly reduced Pain Catastrophizing Scale scores compared to placebo in fibromyalgia patients.
DAO supplementation produced clinically meaningful improvement in overall fibromyalgia impact (FIQ) compared to placebo.
DAO supplementation markedly improved gastrointestinal symptoms (bloating, abdominal discomfort) relative to placebo in the RCT.
DAO supplementation was well-tolerated in the RCT with no significant adverse events, though mild transient GI symptoms occurred in a minority of treated patients.
A histamine-restricted diet based on histamine release testing improved gastrointestinal and systemic symptoms in fibromyalgia patients compared to standard dietary advice.
Fibromyalgia is significantly more prevalent among patients with chronic pruritus than among controls without pruritus.
Fibromyalgia patients experienced more severe pruritus than pruritus patients without fibromyalgia, with chronic duration paralleling the fibromyalgia course.

A large 21-year population study found fibromyalgia patients had significantly increased risk of multiple allergic/histamine-mediated comorbidities, remaining significant after adjustment for confounders.
The majority of fibromyalgia patients with documented DAO deficiency experience significant gastrointestinal symptoms.
Irritable bowel syndrome is highly prevalent among fibromyalgia patients, suggesting shared histamine-related mechanisms with GI motility and visceral sensitivity.
A large proportion of patients with insomnia-related symptoms show genetic DAO deficiency, consistent with histamine's role in sleep-wake regulation.
Multiple studies report increased mast cell degranulation in skin biopsies and elevated serum tryptase in fibromyalgia patients, with some responding to mast cell stabilizers.
PET imaging studies have directly visualized microglial activation in fibromyalgia patients, providing evidence for central neuroinflammation potentially linked to histamine.
Proposed clinical DAO activity thresholds stratify severe deficiency, moderate deficiency, and normal levels, though these thresholds require further validation.
In animal models, cortical spreading depression increased extracellular hydrogen peroxide levels in the cerebral cortex by approximately 20%.
Cortical spreading depression increased cerebral cortex malondialdehyde (a lipid peroxidation marker) concentrations by nearly 67% in animal models.
Meningeal tissue MDA levels may increase by approximately 70% during CSD, indicating oxidative damage in structures involved in migraine pain generation.

Migraine patients show reduced activity of several mitochondrial enzymes (monoamine oxidase, succinate dehydrogenase, NADH dehydrogenase, cyclooxygenase, citrate synthase) in platelets, supporting systemic mitochondrial dysfunction.
31P-MRS studies show abnormalities in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation in migraine patients both during attacks and interictally, indicating persistent cerebral energy metabolism alterations.

In a 25-year cohort of 5620 individuals aged 33–65, migraine with aura at baseline was associated with more than double the risk of developing Parkinson's disease compared with those without headaches (2.4% vs 1.1%).
Nearly 20% of participants with migraine with aura reported multiple parkinsonian symptoms, a higher proportion than in those with migraine without aura or no headache history.
Women with migraine with aura more frequently reported a family history of Parkinson's disease, suggesting shared biological susceptibility.

Riboflavin (vitamin B2) has demonstrated efficacy in clinical trials for migraine prevention, thought to act by enhancing mitochondrial energy metabolism and supporting glutathione recycling to reduce oxidative stress.
Magnesium deficiency has frequently been reported in migraine patients.
Magnesium supplementation may inhibit cortical spreading depression by blocking neuronal calcium channels and reducing neuronal hyperexcitability.

CGRP-targeting monoclonal antibodies (eptinezumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, erenumab) show significant efficacy in reducing migraine frequency and are generally well tolerated, especially in patients refractory to conventional preventives.
The experimental TRPA1 antagonist GRC17536 is under investigation as a potential future migraine therapy targeting oxidative stress-linked trigeminovascular activation.
Amitriptyline treatment has been associated with reduced oxidative stress markers and increased antioxidant capacity in migraine.
Valproate may exert beneficial effects on mitochondrial function in migraine and has been shown to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis.

Administration of nitroglycerin or other NO-releasing compounds can reliably induce delayed migraine-like attacks in susceptible individuals, supporting a causal role for NO in migraine and providing a widely used experimental model.

Under oxidative stress or BH4 cofactor deficiency, NOS enzymes may become uncoupled and produce superoxide instead of nitric oxide, reducing NO bioavailability and contributing to endothelial dysfunction in migraine.
Migraine patients show reduced endothelium-dependent vasodilation (via flow-mediated dilation) compared to healthy controls, indicating impaired vascular reactivity.
Migraine, particularly with aura, is consistently associated with increased risk of ischemic stroke and other vascular events in epidemiological studies.
Migraine and fibromyalgia frequently co-occur and are thought to share neurobiological mechanisms including central sensitization, neuroinflammation, and altered pain processing networks.

Fibromyalgia patients show endocrine abnormalities including dysregulation of the HPA and HPT axes, with altered cortisol, growth hormone, insulin-like growth factor, and thyroid-related hormone levels reported in some patients.

Headaches, including migraine-like headaches, are reported more frequently in Sjögren's disease patients than in the general population, potentially reflecting immune-mediated neuroinflammation or vascular dysfunction.
NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which mediates IL-1β and IL-18 release, has been proposed as a mechanism linking inflammation to migraine, primarily based on preclinical models.
Activated microglia release pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6) that increase neuronal excitability and promote central sensitization in experimental migraine models.
Serum levels of urea, glutamate, valine, taurine, proline, glycine, and homoserine were increased in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls.
Serum levels of benzoate, leucine, π-methylhistidine, galactitol, τ-methylhistidine, glutamine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, and fructose were decreased in fibromyalgia patients relative to healthy controls.

Urinary levels of malate, dimethylamine, trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), creatine phosphate, N-phenylacetylglycine, N-acetylglutamate, hippurate, and urea were increased in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls.
Urinary levels of guanidoacetate, creatine, malonate, serine, glucuronate, creatinine, and uracil were decreased in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls.
Serum glutamate was positively correlated with waist/hip ratio in fibromyalgia patients.
Serum glutamate was negatively correlated with Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) score.
Skin manifestations were the most frequent MCA symptom category, occurring in 100% of the 44 pediatric patients.
Gastrointestinal symptoms were the second most frequent manifestation, occurring in 93% of patients, including abdominal pain (86.3%) and chronic diarrhea (65.9%).
Two distinct clinical profiles of pediatric-onset MCAD were identified based on age at symptom onset, before versus after age 3 years.
Chronic persistent symptoms were significantly more prevalent in children with symptom onset before age 3 than in those with onset at or after age 3.
Chronic diarrhea was significantly more common in the early-onset (<3 years) group than the later-onset group.
Idiopathic anaphylactic reactions were significantly more frequent in the later-onset (≥3 years) group compared to the early-onset group.
Hereditary alpha tryptasemia (HαT), caused by TPSAB1 germline copy number variation, was found in 15.2% of tested patients, significantly higher than the reported general population prevalence.
Baseline serum tryptase levels were significantly higher in patients with hereditary alpha tryptasemia compared to those without.
Serum tryptase rose substantially during acute MCA episodes in the subset of idiopathic MCAS patients tested, consistent with mast cell activation criteria.
Combination treatment with second-generation H1/H2 antihistamines and a leukotriene receptor antagonist was well tolerated and produced significant symptom improvement and quality-of-life gains.
Night-time awakenings, a common sleep disturbance in this cohort, were dramatically reduced (100%) with mast-cell-targeted treatment.
Bone marrow aspirates performed in the first 16 enrolled patients showed no atypical mast cells, no CD2+/CD25+ mast cells, and no KIT mutations, supporting a non-clonal mast cell disorder.
School absenteeism due to MCA symptoms was common, affecting half of school-age children in the cohort.
Among children who underwent upper GI endoscopy, half were found to have a secondary (non-genetic) sucrase-isomaltase deficiency associated with broad food-triggered symptoms.
Food was the most frequent trigger of MCA symptoms, with more than five implicated foods in half the patients, leading to drastically limited diets.
Idiopathic anaphylaxis, unrelated to IgE-mediated food allergy, occurred in over a third of patients and often required epinephrine treatment.
The mean diagnostic delay for pediatric non-mastocytosis MCAD was approximately 3 years, reflecting low awareness of this entity among physicians.
The pediatric non-mastocytosis MCAD cohort showed a slight female predominance.
Large RCTs (ASTERIA I/II, GLACIAL) and real-world studies show omalizumab consistently reduces UAS7 scores and improves CU-specific quality of life, often within 1-2 weeks.
A retrospective longitudinal cohort of 386 omalizumab-treated CSU patients showed progressively increasing cumulative response rates over time.
The omalizumab biosimilar CT-P39 showed therapeutic equivalence to reference omalizumab for weekly itch severity score change in a phase III trial.
A low baseline total IgE level (<40 kU/L) is consistently identified as a predictor of poor omalizumab response in CSU.
Ligelizumab showed numerically greater UAS7 reductions than omalizumab in phase III trials but did not consistently achieve superiority on primary endpoints, halting its clinical development for CSU.

YH35324, a first-in-class IgE Trap-Tc fusion protein, was well tolerated in a phase 1 trial with no dose-limiting toxicities and produced rapid, sustained suppression of free IgE and FcɛRI expression.
Fenebrutinib, a first-generation oral BTK inhibitor, showed efficacy in a phase II trial for H1AH-refractory CSU but its clinical development was discontinued due to hepatotoxicity.
Phase III REMIX-1/REMIX-2 trials showed remibrutinib produced rapid, significant reductions in urticaria activity versus placebo, with well-controlled and complete-control rates at week 12.
Rilzabrutinib 1200 mg/day significantly improved UAS7 scores versus placebo at week 12 in a phase II trial, with reductions in IL-31, soluble MRGPRX2, and autoantibodies.
A systematic review found low-dose cyclosporine (≤3 mg/kg/day) response rates of ~54% at 4 weeks and ~73% at 12 weeks in CSU, with significant improvements in UAS7 and quality of life vs placebo.
In LIBERTY-CSU CUPID phase III trials, dupilumab significantly improved UAS7 and quality of life versus placebo, with up to 30% of omalizumab-naïve patients achieving complete response at week 24.
A phase IIb trial of benralizumab failed to demonstrate clinical efficacy in CSU despite complete eosinophil depletion, suggesting a limited role for eosinophils in CSU pathogenesis.
The phase IIb INCEPTION trial of anti-TSLP tezepelumab in H1AH-refractory CSU did not show a clinically meaningful benefit over placebo.

Barzolvolimab, an anti-c-kit monoclonal antibody, induced apoptosis and sustained dermal mast cell depletion with marked tryptase reduction, and significantly improved UAS7/UCT scores, with up to 71% complete response at 52 weeks.
Anti-heat shock protein 10 (HSP10) IgG autoantibodies are elevated in CSU patients and correlate with disease activity and PAF-dependent mast cell degranulation.
Serum PAF levels are significantly higher and PAF-acetylhydrolase activity lower in CSU patients than healthy controls, with the highest PAF concentrations found among H1AH non-responders.
Basophils in CSU show increased expression of the activation marker CD203c compared to healthy controls.
Circulating basophil counts are often reduced (basopenia) in active CSU, correlating with disease severity.
Skin biopsies from severe or H1AH-refractory CSU patients show increased MRGPRX2 expression in lesional mast cells versus healthy controls, and elevated serum levels correlate with disease activity.

In a longitudinal cohort using data-driven clustering, female sex and IgE sensitization to house dust mites were identified as independent predictors of unfavorable prognosis in chronic urticaria, along with higher disease activity predicting prolonged disease course.

An international real-world registry of chronic urticaria reported that women, particularly those aged 30-65 years, tend to have more severe and refractory CSU with greater disease burden and healthcare utilization.
A meta-analysis showed adding an LTRA (e.g., montelukast) to H1AH therapy modestly reduced urticaria severity and improved quality of life without increasing adverse events.

Lirentelimab, a Siglec-8 monoclonal antibody, showed clinical activity in early-phase trials but subsequent phase III studies in eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease failed their primary endpoints, and further CSU development was not pursued.
Serum and urinary VEGF, sFlt-1, and PlGF were increased even in normoalbuminuric type 2 diabetic patients compared with healthy controls.
In multivariable analysis, serum VEGF correlated directly with UACR, urinary synaptopodin, NAG, and serum P-selectin across all groups of type 2 DM patients.
Serum sFlt-1 correlated directly with UACR, synaptopodin, podocalyxin, NAG, and KIM-1 in multivariable analysis.
Serum PlGF correlated negatively with eGFR and directly with UACR, synaptopodin, and KIM-1 in multivariable analysis.
Urinary VEGF correlated negatively with eGFR and positively with UACR, synaptopodin, podocalyxin, NAG, and KIM-1 in multivariable analysis, the strongest model in the study.
Urinary sFlt-1 correlated negatively with eGFR and directly with UACR, synaptopodin, and podocalyxin in multivariable analysis.
Urinary PlGF correlated negatively with eGFR and directly with UACR, synaptopodin, NAG, and urinary P-selectin in multivariable analysis.
Carotid intima-media thickness (IMT-CCA) correlated inversely with eGFR and directly with UACR, serum P-selectin, and serum sFlt-1.
Pulsatility index in the internal carotid arteries (PI-ICAs) correlated inversely with eGFR and directly with UACR, synaptopodin, serum P-selectin, and serum sFlt-1.
Pulsatility index in the middle cerebral arteries (PI-MCAs) showed an inverse correlation with eGFR and a direct correlation with synaptopodin, serum P-selectin, and serum sFlt-1.
Resistivity index in the internal carotid arteries (RI-ICAs) correlated negatively with eGFR and positively with UACR, synaptopodin, NAG, KIM-1, urinary sFlt-1, and serum PlGF.
Resistivity index in the middle cerebral arteries (RI-MCAs) showed an inverse correlation with eGFR and a direct correlation with NAG, KIM-1, and serum sFlt-1.

Breath-holding index (a measure of cerebrovascular reactivity) correlated directly with eGFR and negatively with serum P-selectin and serum PlGF, suggesting a potentially protective/adaptive role of PlGF in cerebrovascular reactivity.

Carotid IMT, pulsatility and resistivity indices in the internal carotid and middle cerebral arteries were increased, while the breath-holding index (cerebrovascular reactivity) was decreased in type 2 DM patients compared to healthy controls.
IL-6 is consistently elevated in keloid tissue and keloid-derived fibroblasts compared with normal skin and non-pathological scars.
High levels of TNF-α are associated with keloid lesions, promoting immune cell recruitment, sustained inflammatory signaling, and fibroblast activation.
Overexpression of TGF-β signaling in keloids and hypertrophic scars contributes to excessive collagen deposition and impaired extracellular matrix remodeling.

TGF-β signaling through SMAD2/3 stimulates fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation, enhances ECM production, and inhibits apoptosis, sustaining fibroblast activity in a feedback loop with IL-6/JAK-STAT3 signaling.
IL-17 signaling and Th17 cell infiltration have been identified in keloid tissue, suggesting a central role for the Th17/IL-17 axis in keloid pathogenesis.
Mast cells contribute to pathological scarring by releasing histamine, proteases, and pro-fibrotic mediators that enhance fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix deposition.
Substance P and CGRP, neuropeptides released from cutaneous sensory nerves, promote vasodilation, immune cell recruitment, and mast cell activation, amplifying local dermal inflammatory responses.
Mast cell activation amplifies neurogenic inflammation by releasing histamine, cytokines, proteases, and vasoactive mediators that further intensify tissue-level immune signaling.
Substance P directly influences stromal remodeling, enhancing collagen remodeling and altering matrix-regulatory gene expression through neurokinin-1 receptor signaling in human cells.

Psychosocial stress is associated with keloid formation and may contribute to immune dysregulation by stimulating pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic signaling pathways rather than acting solely through behavioral mechanisms.

Depression and anxiety in keloid patients are associated with chronic low-grade systemic inflammation, with elevated IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP that overlap with cytokine profiles seen in scarring conditions.
Patients with keloids experience disproportionately higher rates of depression and anxiety compared to patients with other chronic dermatological disorders.

Polymorphisms in genes involved in collagen synthesis, TGF-β signaling, and inflammatory cytokine regulation have been linked to abnormal fibroblast activation and excessive ECM deposition, predisposing to keloid formation, particularly in individuals of African, Asian, and Hispanic descent.
Dysregulation of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity in keloids and hypertrophic scars impairs collagen degradation, contributing to excessive matrix accumulation.
Surgical excision alone for keloids carries a high risk of recurrence, and even multimodal combined therapy shows substantial and highly variable recurrence rates.
Chronic HPA axis activation alters cortisol signaling pathways and glucocorticoid receptor sensitivity, promoting immune activation rather than resolution in scar tissue.
In vitro studies show elevated IL-6 promotes fibroblast differentiation, apoptosis resistance, and increased collagen synthesis compared to normal dermal fibroblasts.

The authors developed the mCAS cohort of 2,019 Chinese individuals aged 18-91 and built a three-tiered aging framework comprising a core capacity clock, a multimodal clock, and organ-associated aging clocks.
Cross-layer analysis showed that plasma protein-based aging clocks not only track chronological age but also serve as efficient proxies for systemic physiological capacity.
The study identified an age-dependent accumulation of coagulation factors as a driver of multi-organ senescence and systemic inflammatory activation.
The patient exhibited elevated serum IgG autoantibodies against M3/M4 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors and β1/β2-adrenergic receptors, consistent with an autoimmune ME/CFS phenotype.
After three sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange spaced two months apart, muscarinic and adrenergic receptor autoantibody titers significantly decreased.

Therapeutic plasma exchange produced marked and sustained improvement in fatigue, concentration, and cognitive clarity, allowing discontinuation of raltegravir without symptom recurrence at 3- and 6-month follow-up.
Off-label raltegravir 800 mg/day produced marked symptom relief after approximately four months of treatment in this ME/CFS patient.

Following SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2022 while on raltegravir therapy, the patient experienced transient post-exertional malaise and persistent brain fog/concentration difficulties, followed by declining treatment efficacy, suggesting post-infectious immune activation.
A four-week discontinuation of raltegravir led to gradual recurrence of fatigue and elevated autoantibody titers, supporting an autoimmune mechanism underlying the patient's ME/CFS.
The patient was diagnosed with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) in addition to ME/CFS.

The authors propose that plasma exchange may remove pathogenic plasma components such as pro-inflammatory mediators and fibrin amyloid microclots that have been increasingly implicated in post-COVID and ME/CFS pathophysiology.

Oakes et al. found no significant difference in HERV-K18 env transcript levels or HHV-6/HHV-7 viral loads in PBMCs between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls, with no correlation to symptom severity.

Immunohistology of duodenal biopsies showed HERV-K gag and env proteins (HERV-K18.1, HERV-FRD, HERV-R) present in 8 of 12 ME patients but absent in 8 controls, co-localising with plasmacytoid dendritic cells.
Rodrigues et al. reported statistically higher HERV-K env transcriptional activity in PBMCs from moderate ME/CFS patients compared with healthy controls.
HERV-H, -K, and -W types were overexpressed in immune cells from fibromyalgia patients with or without ME/CFS comorbidity, correlating with elevated IFNβ and IFNγ levels.
SARS-CoV-2 infection increases HERV-W env antigenemia, which together with distinct cytokine profiles discriminates post-COVID condition from ME/CFS or fibromyalgia.
Saliva antibodies against EBV, HHV-6, and HERV-K substantially increased 3-6 months after mild/asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection in both non-vaccinated ME/CFS patients and controls.
ME/CFS patients showed an overall stronger antibody response to latent viruses, including higher EBV EBNA1 IgG titres and higher HERV-K IgG responses, particularly pronounced in female patients.
ME/CFS patients showed higher baseline EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG levels even without prior SARS-CoV-2 infection.

HERV microarray profiling of an all-female cohort found ME/CFS samples had 258 upregulated and 78 downregulated HERV loci, predominantly solitary LTRs from 33 families including HERV-H and HERV-P, distinguishing ME/CFS from FM, co-diagnosed patients, and healthy controls.

In the more severe ME/CFS subgroup, greater HERV dysregulation co-occurred with increased plasma cells and resting CD4 memory T cells alongside decreased γδ T cells and altered immune response gene expression.
Activation of specific HERV loci and immune-related genes positively correlated with ME/CFS diagnosis and with disease symptoms including physical and mental fatigue.
A single reported EBV-seropositive ME/CFS patient later diagnosed with multiple sclerosis showed significant clinical improvement and normalisation of HERV expression following rituximab treatment.

HERV-FRD is highly upregulated in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from COVID-19 patients but not in PBMCs, with senescence-related HERV increases in bronchial epithelial cells potentially contributing to worse outcomes in older patients.
Fifty percent or more of long COVID patients meet ME/CFS diagnostic criteria, and these patients are more functionally impaired than non-ME/CFS long COVID patients.
Infection has been identified as the triggering event for 50% or more of ME/CFS sufferers, though no single pathogen has been consistently identified.
In a phase 2b double-blind trial in relapsing-remitting MS, the anti-HERV-W env monoclonal antibody temelimab failed to reduce acute inflammation but showed promising anti-neurodegenerative effects.
In ALS, most patients treated with a combination of anti-retroviral drugs showed reduced HERV-K levels and slower disease progression trends.
In MS, natalizumab treatment decreased HERV-W env expression in PBMCs.
Cytosolic calcium influx amplitude and slope were significantly reduced, with a shorter half-time response, in NK cells from ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
Mitochondrial calcium influx amplitude and slope in NK cells were significantly higher in ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
In healthy controls, pharmacological activation of TRPM3 with pregnenolone sulfate produced a pronounced cytosolic calcium response accompanied by increased mitochondrial calcium.

TRPM3-dependent cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium mobilisation in NK cells, triggered by pregnenolone sulfate, was significantly reduced with a shorter half-time response in ME/CFS patients compared to healthy controls.
Recent prevalence estimates place ME/CFS at approximately 0.42% of adults in the USA, with high-income-country estimates generally 0.2-1%.
A German study reported 0.78% ME/CFS prevalence and 1.7% for combined post-infectious conditions, with an estimated €64.4 billion annual cost (~1.44% of GDP) in 2025.
A large UK patient survey found frequent diagnostic delay in ME/CFS, with 12.9% waiting more than 10 years for diagnosis and only 10.1% reporting a positive impact from updated NICE guidance.

Following sustained methodological critique of the PACE trial, the 2021 revision of UK clinical guidance removed graded exercise therapy (GET) as a recommended treatment and reframed CBT as supportive rather than curative.

Two-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) showed reproducible impairments in recovery after exertion (reduced oxygen consumption, workload, and anaerobic threshold on repeat testing), providing objective evidence that PEM is a state-dependent physiological failure rather than deconditioning.

A systematic reanalysis of ME/CFS transcriptomic and proteomic datasets found minimal reproducibility at the individual-gene level, with only two genes consistently replicated across studies and little proteomic convergence.
Despite poor gene-level reproducibility, mitochondrial dysregulation emerged as a recurrent, convergent feature across multiple omics data modalities in ME/CFS.
ME/CFS is associated with accelerated biological ageing, including premature telomere attrition in peripheral blood cells, consistent with chronic cumulative cellular stress.

Herpesvirus proteins produced during abortive lytic replication, particularly viral dUTPases, are proposed to drive chronic immune activation independent of productive infection by activating innate immune pathways and inducing pro-inflammatory cytokines.

Circulating soluble factors (cytokines, metabolites, acute-phase proteins) in Long-COVID plasma can drive abnormal fibrin architecture and fibrinolysis resistance even using healthy-donor fibrinogen, supporting a plasma-transferable prothrombotic mechanism.

Purified IgG from Long-COVID patients with neurological sequelae induced pain-related phenotypes upon passive transfer into mice, localising preferentially to dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons, with loss of effect after IgG depletion or enzymatic cleavage.

In ME/CFS patients, circulating fibronectin (Fn1) is increased in serum yet depleted within IgG-bound circulating immune complexes, indicating selective alteration in immune-complex composition rather than a uniform increase.
An independent cohort also found increased circulating fibronectin in the plasma of ME/CFS patients.
Natural IgM antibodies against fibronectin, which normally serve homeostatic scavenger/protector/regulator roles, were found to be depleted after COVID infection.
Patient-derived IgG entering endothelial cells (HUVECs) drove mitochondrial network fragmentation and altered mitochondrial proteins/energetics in a subset of patients, with a sex-stratified signal.

Passive transfer of patient IgG to healthy PBMCs induced secretion of inflammatory cytokines, with IL-1β reaching statistical significance across the cohort, supporting circulating immunoglobulin as a functional effector rather than a passive biomarker.

Endothelial cells exposed to ME/CFS plasma appear normal at rest, but show impaired adaptive capacity (energy production, redox balance, barrier integrity, nitric oxide/mitochondrial signalling) under immune, oxidative, mechanical, or metabolic challenge, indicating a state-dependent rather than constitutive dysfunction.
ATG13, an autophagosome-initiation protein, was markedly elevated in ME/CFS serum across independent cohorts, and exogenous ATG13 triggered inflammatory signalling in vitro.

SMPDL3B, a membrane-associated regulator of sphingolipid balance, is identified as a potential ME/CFS biomarker; its alteration may change lipid raft fluidity and receptor organisation, modifying immune responses.

Haptoglobin quantity and proteoform structure are relevant to core ME/CFS symptoms of PEM and cognitive dysfunction, with reduced functional Hp capacity permitting exaggerated oxidative and vascular stress after exertion.

EV cargo profiling in ME/CFS revealed altered cytokine and proteomic signatures, severity-associated immune cell markers, exercise-induced changes aligned with PEM, and mitochondrial DNA capable of activating innate immune pathways.
Studies have identified distinct monocyte transcriptional and metabolic states in Long-COVID, characterised by altered interferon signalling, inflammatory tone, and metabolic gene expression.

Persistent alterations in monocyte activation profiles following viral infection can outlast viral clearance, constraining immune flexibility and amplifying inflammatory responses to secondary stressors such as exertion or infection.
The proportion of M2-like monocytes was increased in both CFS and long COVID patients relative to healthy controls, with the increase reaching statistical significance only in long COVID.
M2-like monocyte activation marker CD69+CD38 MFI was significantly lower in long COVID patients while CFS levels were comparable to healthy controls.
CD80 costimulatory molecule expression on M2-like monocytes was highest in long COVID, significantly exceeding CFS, with healthy controls at intermediate levels.
CCR7 expression on M2-like monocytes was lowest in CFS compared with long COVID and healthy controls, but the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CD80 expression on M1-like monocytes was increased in long COVID compared to both healthy controls and CFS, with statistical significance versus CFS.
CCR7 expression on M1-like monocytes was significantly decreased in both CFS and long COVID compared with healthy controls, with the reduction most pronounced in CFS.
CD69+CD38 expression on M1-like monocytes trended lower in CFS and long COVID compared to healthy controls but did not reach statistical significance.
The frequency of circulating dendritic cells was significantly highest in long COVID patients, exceeding both CFS and healthy controls.
Dendritic cell activation marker expression (CD38+CD69+) was lower in CFS compared to long COVID.
CD80 expression on dendritic cells was lowest in CFS compared to both long COVID and healthy controls.
CCR7 expression on dendritic cells trended lower in both long COVID and CFS compared with healthy controls.
Patients with moderate disease severity (CFS or long COVID) had significantly higher percentages of CD4+CD62L+ (central memory-associated) T cells compared with healthy controls.
The proportion of naive CD4+CD45RA+ T cells was significantly lower in patients with moderate CFS or long COVID compared with healthy controls.
Composite neuropsychiatric/physiosomatic symptom scores (combining HAM-A, HAM-D, and FibroFatigue) were significantly higher in both CFS and long COVID than in healthy controls.
In moderate long COVID, dendritic cells showed significantly increased CD69+CD38 activation marker expression but decreased CD80 expression compared to mild cases and healthy controls.
In moderate CFS, dendritic cells showed significantly increased CD69+CD38 expression and decreased CD80 expression compared to mild cases and healthy controls.

PCA-derived innate immune activation component (Component 1, dominated by monocyte HLA-DR and CD80 loadings) was significantly and inversely associated with anxiety symptom severity, independent of age and sex.
PCA-derived T cell differentiation component (Component 2) was positively associated with anxiety symptom severity, independent of age and sex.
The innate immune activation component (Component 1) showed a strong negative association with depression severity, independent of age.
The T cell differentiation component (Component 2) was positively associated with depression severity, and sex was also a significant predictor in this model.
The T cell differentiation component (Component 2) was a significant positive predictor of fatigue severity, though the overall regression model for fatigue was not statistically significant.

A PLS-DA model using the immune biomarker panel discriminated long COVID from CFS/healthy controls with moderate accuracy (~69%) and AUC of 0.758, validated by permutation testing as better than chance.
CFS patients had a significantly longer median duration since symptom onset than long COVID patients.
Using the HEAL2 deep learning framework on whole-genome sequencing data, researchers identified 115 high-confidence ME/CFS risk genes enriched in CNS and immune-related biological pathways.
The HEAL2 model predicted ME/CFS risk from genome-wide rare variant burden with an AUROC of 0.67 on an independent cohort, with no single gene dominating prediction.
The DecodeME GWAS, comparing 15,579 ME/CFS cases to 259,909 healthy controls, identified eight loci significantly associated with ME/CFS, linked to immune and nervous system disruption.
A GWAS locus near OLFM4 was associated specifically with ME/CFS patients who reported an infection at illness onset, suggesting a genetic link to post-infectious triggering.
A GWAS locus near CA10 shares genetic signals with chronic pain, a symptom reported by over 86% of ME/CFS cases in the DecodeME study.
DecodeME found a lack of genetic colocalization between ME/CFS risk loci and depression or anxiety, molecularly distinguishing ME/CFS from psychiatric conditions.

A longitudinal study of ME/CFS patients across relapse and recovery found that variations in the DNA methylome correlated directly with symptom severity, with methylation changes occurring in metabolic, immune, and inflammatory gene regulatory regions during relapse.

Circulating plasma cytokine studies in ME/CFS patients have shown high levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNFα) alongside elevated anti-inflammatory/regulatory cytokines such as TGF-β.
Increased plasma levels of CSF2 (GM-CSF) and TNFα were associated with increased physical impairment and fatigue in ME/CFS patients.

RNA-seq of PBMCs collected during CPET-induced PEM showed sex-specific transcriptomic responses: male ME/CFS patients exhibited an unregulated IL-12 signaling cascade sustained through recovery, while females showed enrichment of HSV-1 reactivation pathways during recovery.

Single-cell transcriptomics revealed significant upregulation of the exhaustion transcription factors TOX and EOMES in CD8+ T cells of ME/CFS patients, consistent with durable, epigenetically encoded T cell exhaustion.
Exhausted CD8+ T cells in ME/CFS patients show increased surface expression of inhibitory receptors PD-1 and SLAMF6, functionally repressing T cell activation.
ME/CFS immune cells exhibit significantly lowered mitochondrial coupling efficiency, meaning oxygen consumption is not effectively converted to ATP, resulting in wasted, 'uncoupled' respiration.
Proteomic analysis identified dysregulation of enzymes governing PDH and CoA metabolism, suggesting a metabolic bottleneck preventing efficient fuel entry into the mitochondrial TCA cycle in ME/CFS.
Longitudinal proteomics 24 hours post-exertion showed depletion of structural muscle proteins MYBPC1 and MYL3, suggesting direct disruption of neuromuscular integrity during PEM recovery failure.

The molecular pattern of post-exertional proteomic recovery is sex-specific: females show heightened expression of thousands of proteins (disordered pattern), while males show a hyporesponsive pattern during recovery.

Positive Unlabeled Learning applied to single-cell data identified a diseased monocyte subset overexpressing CCL4, suggesting these monocytes are pathologically primed for tissue infiltration and inflammation in ME/CFS.

The proportion of diseased to normal monocytes varied widely between ME/CFS patients and was strongly correlated with clinical severity metrics including MFI-20 fatigue score, general health, and PEM severity.

Plasma cfRNA analysis in 93 ME/CFS patients versus 75 healthy controls identified 743 differentially expressed transcripts, later distilled by machine learning to a 21-gene subset including HNRNPLL and TGFB2.

Misclassified cfRNA samples in the diagnostic model were strongly associated with aberrant proportions of platelet-derived cfRNA, suggesting baseline platelet dysfunction as a confounding biological factor in ME/CFS.
High-density microarray profiling of over 305,000 HERV elements in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia patients established a direct correlation between ME/CFS symptom severity and HERV deregulation.
Digital cytometry deconvolution (CIBERSORTx) showed HERV dysregulation was strongly correlated with depletion of gamma delta T cells and expansion of resting CD4 memory T cells and plasma cells.

Supervised machine learning integrating plasma proteomics, cytokines, and EV cytokine cargo identified a 20-protein diagnostic panel (from 353 analytes) distinguishing ME/CFS from healthy controls with 86.1% accuracy (AUC=0.947).
A consensus seven-protein signature including increased EV IL-2 and CAMP with reduced structural proteins including tubulin maintained 79.1% diagnostic accuracy across models for ME/CFS.

A LightGBM machine learning model applied to UK Biobank NMR metabolomics from 1194 ME/CFS patients versus seven comorbid disease groups and controls distilled data to a 28-feature set that detected ME/CFS with AUC=0.83 and recall=0.70.

SHAP explainability analysis of the UK Biobank metabolomic model found lower VLDL particle levels among the strongest contributors to the ME/CFS disease signature, alongside physical fatigue measures.

The BioMapAI explainable AI model, integrating gut metagenomics, metabolomics, and immune profiling, found that gut-host metabolic cross-talk through tryptophan and butyrate pathways is mechanistically linked to ME/CFS pain and fatigue symptomatology.
Two-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) showed that ME/CFS cohorts exhibit a significant drop in peak oxygen consumption (VO2 peak/VO2 max) on the second day compared to the first.
Elevated neopterin levels, a byproduct of activated monocytes and macrophages, have been identified as an inflammation biomarker in ME/CFS patients.
CSF Norepinephrine Pathway activity was significantly lower in post-infectious ME/CFS patients compared to healthy volunteers.
CSF Norepinephrine Pathway activity was significantly lower in PASC (long COVID) patients compared to healthy volunteers.
CSF Norepinephrine Pathway activity was significantly lower in Parkinson's disease patients (used as positive controls) compared to healthy volunteers.
PASC participants with post-exertional malaise showed evidence of central noradrenergic deficiency compared to healthy volunteers.
CSF Dopamine Pathway activity did not differ between the ME/CFS or PASC groups and healthy volunteers.
Across all participants, higher Norepinephrine Pathway activity correlated with longer handgrip duration, a measure of physical function.
Across all participants, higher Norepinephrine Pathway activity correlated with better self-reported general health.
Across all participants, lower Norepinephrine Pathway activity correlated with greater fatigue.

Heritability estimates for functional somatic syndromes (including ME/CFS, fibromyalgia, IBS) and internalizing disorders (major depression, anxiety) ranged from 15-44%, with unique environmental factors explaining the majority (49-84%) of variance.
Heritability of immune-mediated (autoimmune and autoinflammatory) diseases was estimated at 37%, with a unique environmental component of 63%.
Fibromyalgia showed the strongest genetic correlation with immune-mediated diseases among the functional somatic syndromes and internalizing disorders examined.
ME/CFS showed a modest genetic correlation with immune-mediated diseases, in the range shared with IBS and major depression.
IBS showed a modest genetic correlation with immune-mediated diseases, in the range shared with ME/CFS and major depression.
Major depression showed a modest genetic correlation with immune-mediated diseases, in the range shared with IBS and ME/CFS.
Anxiety disorders showed minimal genetic correlation with immune-mediated diseases, notably lower than fibromyalgia and other functional somatic syndromes.
A total of 27 distinct mental-health-related registry variables were longitudinally associated with subsequent diagnosis of IBS, CFS, or FM, with 25 linked to IBS, 10 to CFS, and 20 to FM.
Prior registrations for anxiety, psychosis, addiction behavior, and concentration disorders each showed positive predictive value for later diagnosis of IBS, CFS, and FM alike.
Having a prior mental health-related referral was inversely (negatively) predictive of subsequent diagnosis of IBS, CFS, and FM.
A logistic LASSO regression model using mental health-related registrations predicted subsequent IBS diagnosis with fair classification performance (AUC = 0.77).
A logistic LASSO regression model using mental health-related registrations predicted subsequent CFS diagnosis with good classification performance (AUC = 0.82).
A logistic LASSO regression model using mental health-related registrations predicted subsequent FM diagnosis with good classification performance (AUC = 0.88).

The reviewed empirical literature supports a clinical and phenomenological overlap between long-COVID, chronic fatigue syndrome, and fibromyalgia, though the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
Studies on new-onset post-COVID fibromyalgia report conflicting findings regarding the presence of residual viral particles as a possible mechanistic driver.
Studies on new-onset post-COVID fibromyalgia report conflicting findings regarding central sensitization as a mechanistic feature.
Studies on new-onset post-COVID fibromyalgia report conflicting findings regarding the presence of autoantibodies as a possible mechanistic driver.

The authors propose an integrative pathophysiological model framing fibromyalgia and multisystem medically-unexplained manifestations of long-COVID as a non-autoimmune connective tissue disease, offered as a theory-based hypothesis for future testing.

In an elderly woman with pre-existing rheumatoid arthritis, COVID-19 infection or subsequent AstraZeneca vaccination appeared to trigger a flare of arthritis with severe lower limb manifestations and sacroiliitis.
The patient developed herpes infection (herpetic lesions) secondary to rheumatoid arthritis following COVID-19 infection or vaccination, with associated increased susceptibility to herpes.
The patient reported chronic fatigue syndrome symptoms co-occurring with post-COVID mood disturbance, severe pain, and herpetic lesions.
Despite an integrative pharmacologic and complementary treatment regimen for arthritis, herpes, and mood symptoms, the patient's clinical condition did not improve.
Family-based whole-exome sequencing identified a CD44 splice-site variant (c.1516+1G>A) present in all affected members of a three-generation hEDS family.
An ITIH2 variant (c.783C>G) was identified in all affected members of the hEDS family via whole-exome sequencing.
An ADAM21 variant (c.397C>T) was identified in all affected members of the hEDS family via whole-exome sequencing.
Among 22 unrelated hEDS patients, WES identified 114 variants across 103 candidate genes, suggesting genetic heterogeneity underlying hEDS.

17 of the 22 unrelated hEDS patients carried variants in genes belonging to the same biological pathways as the family-derived causative genes (CD44, ITIH2, ADAM21), suggesting pathway-level convergence.
The hEDS cohort showed a significantly greater manual anterior drawer test (ADT) grade compared with healthy controls, indicating clinically detectable ankle instability.
Anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) length, both at rest and under stress, was significantly greater in hEDS patients than in controls, measured by stress ultrasonography.
Women with hEDS maintained overall adequate bone mineral density at the spine and femur despite the condition's connective tissue frailty.
Despite adequate bone mineral density, half of the hEDS patients had experienced a fracture as an adult, and three were osteopenic.
Higher pain levels were strongly associated with lower PROMIS-10 mental health scores in women with hEDS.
Higher pain levels were strongly associated with lower PROMIS-10 physical function scores in women with hEDS.
Greater kinesiophobia (fear of movement) was moderately associated with lower mental health scores in women with hEDS.
Greater kinesiophobia was strongly associated with lower physical function scores in women with hEDS.
GI problems were significantly associated with food allergies in the path analysis model.
GI problems were significantly associated with fearful eating behaviors.
GI problems were significantly associated with painful eating behaviors.
GI problems were significantly associated with somatosensory amplification (heightened perception of bodily sensations).
Painful eating was positively associated with fearful eating behaviors.
Fearful eating was positively associated with avoidant/restrictive eating behaviors.
Rare coding variants in COL1A1 were identified in 5 of the 272 early-onset BAV probands.
Rare coding variants in COL1A2 were identified in 5 of the 272 early-onset BAV probands.
Overall, rare predicted damaging COL1 variants were found in 10 of 272 (4%) EBAV probands, representing a 30-fold enrichment compared with European ancestry population reference data.
Only two of the ten identified COL1 variants involved glycine substitutions within the triple-helical domain, the mutation type classically associated with osteogenesis imperfecta.
The COL1 variants found in EBAV probands affected different residues than those typically causing osteogenesis imperfecta, suggesting a distinct pathogenic mechanism despite phenotypic overlap.

An 18-year-old woman with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome developed a lateral circumflex femoral artery pseudoaneurysm with arteriovenous fistula as a vascular complication 21 days after hip arthroscopy and periacetabular osteotomy.
Endovascular coil embolization combined with thrombin injection achieved complete thrombosis of the pseudoaneurysm and resolution of the patient's symptoms.

The authors conclude that vascular injury, though rare, should be considered after hip arthroscopy in patients with connective tissue disorders, and that early multimodal imaging enables timely diagnosis.
A homozygous splice-site variant in AEBP1 (c.1401-2A>G) was identified as the causal genetic lesion in this patient with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome classical-like type 2.
Transcript analysis showed that the AEBP1 splice-site variant causes complete skipping of exon 12, producing a frameshift and predicted loss of AEBP1 function.

The patient experienced postoperative sigmoid colon perforation shortly after rectal cancer surgery and, nearly 20 years later, a spontaneous small intestinal perforation, illustrating gastrointestinal fragility in clEDS2.
Histopathology of the affected colonic tissue showed mildly widened intermuscular spaces without other overt structural abnormalities, providing a tissue-level correlate of GI fragility in clEDS2.

Despite repeated upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopic procedures during long-term oncological surveillance, no procedure-related bowel perforation occurred, suggesting AEBP1-related clEDS2 GI fragility differs in clinical context from vascular EDS.
A 34-year-old man with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome developed spontaneous splenic artery rupture presenting as sudden abdominal pain with rapid progression to hemorrhagic shock.
Endovascular coil embolization of the splenic artery via a left humeral approach achieved hemostasis and produced immediate clinical improvement in a VEDS patient with splenic artery rupture.
The David valve-sparing aortic root replacement procedure showed a 100% survival rate at 20 years with minimal complications or reoperations in patients with connective tissue disorders.
The Bentall composite valve graft procedure showed high durability with a 94% survival rate over 20 years in patients with connective tissue disorders.
General (non-specialized) surgical approaches showed lower survival and reoperation-free rates than specialized techniques, particularly in aortic dissection cases.
Meta-analysis showed valve-sparing surgical techniques produced superior outcomes compared to composite valve grafting, with fewer complications such as thromboembolism and hemorrhage.
Scoliosis correction surgery in Marfan syndrome patients led to a significant reduction in spinal curvature, improving musculoskeletal outcomes.
Quantitative sensory testing showed no significant differences in pain sensitivity or pain thresholds between youth with chronic pain plus hypermobility disorder and those with chronic pain alone.
Youth with chronic pain and comorbid hypermobility disorder reported greater spatial spread of pain compared to those with chronic pain alone.
Youth with chronic pain and comorbid hypermobility disorder reported increased fatigue compared to those with chronic pain alone.
Youth with chronic pain and comorbid hypermobility disorder reported poorer sleep quality compared to those with chronic pain alone.

Task-evoked fMRI during a multisensory task showed group differences in cerebellar activation between youth with chronic pain plus hypermobility disorder and those with chronic pain alone, though this was only significant at one of two study sites.

Baseline functional connectivity between the cerebellum and supplementary motor cortex differed between youth with chronic pain plus hypermobility disorder and those with chronic pain alone, again only at one of two study sites.

The authors identified the GZF1 c.1440del variant in homozygosity in two affected sisters and in compound heterozygosity with c.1451_1452del in a third patient, expanding the molecular spectrum of GZF1-related phenotype.

The three new patients presented with severe ophthalmologic phenotypes, including congenital glaucoma and abnormal iris morphology, supporting the ocular severity that distinguishes GZF1-related phenotype from Larsen syndrome.
New radiological findings were identified in GZF1-related phenotype, including cervical segmentation defects, carpal shortening, and lower lumbar sacralization.
